title: Retrieving a Newly Added Carrier from eHub
content:
Overview
When a new carrier is added on your eHub account, it does not automatically appear in Logiwa IO. To make the new carrier and its services available, you need to trigger a refresh from the eHub carrier setup screen in Logiwa IO. This article walks you through the steps.
When to Use It
You have just added a new carrier on your eHub account and want it to be available in Logiwa IO.
A new carrier service has been enabled on eHub and is not yet visible in Logiwa IO.
You expect to see updated carrier or service options in the
Services
tab but they are missing.
Prerequisites
The new carrier is fully added and configured on your
eHub account
.
Your user account has access to
Integrations > Shipping
.
Step-by-Step Instructions
Log in to Logiwa IO.
Navigate to
Integrations > Shipping
.
Select
eHub
and open the related carrier setup. The
Carrier Setup
drawer opens on the right side of the screen.
In the Carrier Setup drawer, click the
Services
tab.
Locate the
Give access to all existing and future services
option.
If selected,
unselect
it. This is required so that the system shows the explicit list of carriers and services, allowing the new entries to be visible.
If already unselected, leave it as-is and continue.
Click the
refresh icon
next to the
Bulk Actions
button.
Logiwa IO calls eHub and pulls the latest list of carriers and services configured on your account.
The newly added carrier and its services now appear in the list below, ready to be enabled or configured as needed.
Common Questions & Edge Cases
The new carrier does not appear after I refresh. What should I do?
Confirm that the carrier is fully configured and active on the eHub side, then click the refresh icon again. Logiwa IO retrieves only what eHub returns at the moment of the refresh, so anything not yet active on eHub will not appear.
Why don’t I see any services listed in the Services tab?
Check that
Give access to all existing and future services
is unselected. While this option is selected, individual carriers and services are not displayed.
The refresh fails or times out. How can I fix it?
Verify that your eHub credentials in the Logiwa IO integration settings are still valid. If the credentials are correct and the issue persists, contact Logiwa support.
Will the refresh change services I have already enabled?
Yes — the refresh syncs Logiwa IO with eHub based on the latest API response. Carriers and services that no longer exist on eHub will be removed, and any new ones will be added. Be aware that if a carrier or service has been removed on the eHub side, it will also be removed from Logiwa IO after the refresh.

title: Wave Log Report
content:
Efficient order fulfillment is the backbone of any well-managed warehouse, and wave management is critical in achieving that efficiency. Waves are scheduled processes that automatically batch and allocate orders based on predefined criteria, ensuring optimal picking and packing operations.
Once a wave rule is triggered in the Wave Rules screen, a unique wave number is logged, and its details become accessible through the Wave Log Report. This powerful report allows users to track and analyze wave performance, providing valuable insights to enhance operational workflows and meet fulfillment goals.
Please keep in mind that the allocation process follows these steps:
Wave Rule Filtering
: Unallocated orders are filtered based on Wave Rule Set Conditions, and ineligible orders are eliminated.
Job Type Matching
: Remaining orders are evaluated against Job Type Conditions sequentially. Orders that don't match the job type are eliminated to be checked for the next job type within the wave rule set.
Allocation Attempt
: For orders that meet the job type conditions, the system applies the allocation algorithm of the respective job type. Orders may still be excluded if they fail the order-specific conditions in the algorithm.
Inventory Check
: Finally, the system verifies available inventory based on inventory conditions in the allocation algorithm. Orders meeting all criteria are allocated.
Field Descriptions
Rule Set:
The name defined in the system for each wave rule set.
Wave No:
A unique code the system assigns to each wave that runs.
Wave Status:
The status field displays the current stage of the wave run process.
Failed: Job creation failed due to a technical issue.
In Progress: Job Creation has started, but not finished yet, the system is still allocating orders and creating the jobs.
Pending: Jobs are created by Logiwa and all of the jobs are in pending status, waiting to be started.
Started: Once the first job in the wave is started, the wave status is updated as Started.
Completed: All jobs are completed in the wave.
# of Orders Met Rule Set Criteria:
This number represents the total orders that pass the initial wave filters and align with the specified conditions.
# of Shortage Orders:
Number of orders that were not allocated because the system could not find enough inventory to fulfill the order based on the allocation algorithm.
# of Jobs Created:
Number of jobs created with the orders that the wave allocated.
# of Allocated Orders: Number of orders allocated into jobs with the wave.
Run Date:
The date and time that the wave rule was triggered.
Run By:
The user that the wave rule was triggered by.
Message:
A description of the possible issue with the wave rule set failing. Some examples can be:
“There is no order found by Rule Set” -
There are no open/shortage orders that fit the Rule Set Conditions.
“Another wave in same warehouse is actively creating jobs. Please wait until its status becomes Pending before starting another rule. Running multiple rules concurrently can impact the order allocation process.” -
There can only be 1 active wave rule in process within the same warehouse.
“Jobs could not be optimized by AI” -
Technical issue

title: Serial Numbers Overview and Resources
content:
Serial numbers play a vital role in the efficient management of inventory and accurate record-keeping within Logiwa. By tracking serial numbers, businesses can ensure effective product tracking, identify faulty items, and streamline warranty management processes. This article provides an overview of the usage of serial numbers in the Logiwa system. It covers topics such as the setup of serial number scanning, how they show up during operations, and their tracking within the system.
Serial Number Tracking is supported in Receiving & Packing/Shipment processes in Logiwa IO. In other operation types (such as Transfer, Count, Replenishment, Picking, etc.), only the product's SKU or Barcode will be scanned to complete the operations. The locations of the serial numbers are not being tracked.
NOTE:
Serial number tracking is supported with UOM pack types only.
Serial Number Reports show the received and shipped serial numbers and calculate the serial numbers based on this report in the warehouse.
Enable Serial Number Tracking for a Product
Serial number tracking can be enabled when creating a product or when editing the product after the fact from the
Advanced
section. Serial numbers can be set to be scanned during receiving and packing or only at packing, along with other guidelines.
Learn more about setting up serial numbers for products here:
Create a Product - Serial Number Tracking
Add Inventory for Products with Serial Number Tracking
To manually add inventory to a product with serial number tracking enabled, we recommend using the mobile app.
While it is possible to add inventory using the desktop version of Logiwa if
Scan Serial Number During Packing Only
is enabled for a product, it cannot be done for products with
Scan Serial Number During Receiving and Packing
enabled.
Learn more about manually adding inventory from desktop here:
How to Add Inventory
Transfer Operations
During transfer operations, such as putaway and picking, our system does not require the scanning of serial numbers. This is done in order to streamline the process and increase efficiency, as tracking serial numbers during transfer operations requires additional time and effort from employees.
Serial Number Report
Serial number tracking, shipment history, and receiving history can be viewed from the
Serial Number Report
.
See our dedicated article to learn more
.

title: Kit Inventory Report
content:
Definition
The Kit Inventory Report is designed to provide detailed insights into kit products within the inventory. Kit products can be categorized into two types:
Kit-to-Stock
and
Kit-to-Order
.
Kit-to-Stock
products physically exist in the inventory, whereas
Kit-to-Order
products are assembled on-demand and do not physically exist in the inventory until ordered.
To get more detailed information about kit-to-order products, you may check this article:
Kit-to-Order Product Creation
How is it useful?
This report is essential for inventory management, enabling businesses to track and manage their kit products effectively. It helps in:
Determining the availability of components needed to assemble kits.
Managing inventory levels for both Kit-to-Stock and Kit-to-Order products.
Ensuring timely fulfillment of orders by monitoring pending order quantities.
Optimizing the production and assembly processes based on available resources and inventory.
How does it work?
To improve system performance, this report is generated from a cached data model that updates the report's data in every 15 minutes. The
"Last Updated"
column indicates how recently the data has been refreshed.
​
The report distinguishes between Kit-to-Stock and Kit-to-Order products, providing calculations for inventory capacity and kitting requirements based on available components and existing inventory. This helps in efficient inventory management and timely order fulfillment.
Column Explanations
Field
Description
SKU
The Stock Keeping Unit, a unique identifier for each kit product.
Product Name
The name of the kit product.
Product Barcode
The barcode associated with the kit product.
Kit Type
Indicates whether the kit is a Kit-to-Stock or Kit-to-Order.
Pack Type Name
The type of packaging used for the kit product.
Client
The client associated with the kit product.
Warehouse
The warehouse where the kit product is stored or assembled.
Product Group
The group or category the kit product belongs to.
Product Type
The type of product, further classifying the kit product.
Total Inventory Capacity
Kit-to-Order
: The number of Kit-to-Order products that can be produced from the total quantity of components.
Kit-to-Stock
: The total number of Kit-to-Stock products that can be produced from the toal quantity of components plus the existing KS inventory.
Net Kitting Capacity
Kit-to-Order
: The number of Kit-to-Order products that can be produced from the available components.
Kit-to-Stock
: The number of Kit-to-Stock products that can be produced from the available components.
Pending Order Quantity
The amount required for non-shipped sales orders (SOs) for both Kit-to-Order and Kit-to-Stock products.
Current Inventory Quantity
Kit-to-Order
: Irrelevant and always zero.
Kit-to-Stock
: The existing inventory of Kit-to-Stock products
Required Kitting Quantity
Kit-to-Order
: Always equals to
Pending Order Quantity
(as Kit-to-Order Products cannot physically exist in the inventory)
Kit-to-Stock
: Calculated as the difference between the open SO quantity and the existing inventory.

title: Inventory Snapshot Report
content:
The
Inventory Snapshot Report
provides warehouse managers with a daily snapshot of their inventory, taken once a day at night at the same time. This report helps align inventory data with billing cycles and aids in financial reconciliation. By offering key inventory details, including item dimensions and location information, it enhances decision-making for stock management, space utilization, and overall logistics planning. The report displays data for a maximum of 30 days, ensuring manageable and precise reporting.
Key Features
Daily Inventory Tracking
: Capture a snapshot of your inventory taken automatically once a day, allowing you to track inventory consistently over time.
Comprehensive Details
: Includes vital information such as item dimensions (weight, length, width, and height), inventory status, lot/batch details, and license plate numbers.
Customizable Views
: The report is sortable and filterable, allowing users to customize the data based on specific needs like warehouse, location, or product.
Excel Export
: Easily export data to Excel for further analysis or reporting.
Permission-based Access
: Users can only view the inventory snapshots for warehouses and clients they are authorized to access.
Field
Description
Warehouse
The specific warehouse where the product is stored.
Client
The client or customer associated with the product inventory.
Snapshot Date
The date when the inventory snapshot was captured. Filters are restricted to date ranges of 30 days or less. Invalid filters show clear error messages, and unsupported options are hidden.
SKU
The stock-keeping unit identifier for the product.
Location
The location code within the warehouse where the product is stored.
LP Number
The license plate number associated with the stored product.
UOM Qty
The quantity of the product in its base unit of measure (UOM).
Pack Qty
The quantity of the product based on its pack size.
Lot Batch Number
The lot or batch number associated with the product, if applicable.
Expiry Date
The expiration date of the product, if applicable.
Damage Reason
The reason for any damage noted for the product, if applicable.
Parent LP Number
The license plate number for the parent container or pallet, if applicable.
UOM Pack Type
The type of packaging for the product in its base unit of measure (UOM).
Pack Type
The type of packaging used for the product (e.g., box, pallet, etc.).
Inventory Status
The current status of the inventory, such as available, damaged, or on hold.
Product Weight
The weight of the product.
Product Lenght
The length of the product.
Product Width
The width of the product.
Product Height
The height of the product.
Explanation of the Report's Purpose
The
Inventory Snapshot Report
is designed to provide a comprehensive daily record of inventory levels, locations, and associated details. Captured at the same time every night, this report offers a snapshot of inventory status, helping businesses accurately track stock quantities, packaging types, and product dimensions.
The primary purpose of this report is to:
Assist in Financial Reconciliation
: By aligning daily inventory data with billing cycles, businesses can ensure accurate financial tracking, avoid discrepancies, and optimize billing processes.
Enhance Inventory Management
: The report provides insights into product location, lot/batch numbers, expiry dates, and license plate numbers, enabling more effective management of stock across multiple warehouses.
Support Decision-Making
: The inclusion of detailed product dimensions and statuses allows for better strategic decision-making regarding stock levels, space utilization, and replenishment needs.
Improve Accuracy in Operations
: With this snapshot, users can compare historical data, evaluate inventory status changes, and ensure smooth operations by having detailed records of daily inventory conditions.
This report is particularly valuable for evaluating warehouse performance, making data-driven inventory decisions, and managing billing cycles efficiently.

title: Return Management - Reporting
content:
1. The Return Orders Screen: Managing Return Progress
The
Return Orders
tab, located next to the
Shipped & Canceled
tab on the Shipment Orders screen, is your central hub for viewing and managing active RMAs and direct SO-based returns.
The status of returns is displayed as either
Pending
,
In Transit
,
Started
,
Completed
, or
Cancelled
.
Manually Updating Statuses
You can manually update the status of one or more returns using the
Change Status
button on the Return Orders screen.
Permission Required:
Your user role must have "Update" permission for Return Orders to use this feature.
Bulk Updates:
You can select multiple returns to update at once, but they must all have the same current status.
Understanding the Return Status Lifecycle
Pending
What it means:
An RMA has been created but has not yet been processed.
How it's set:
This is the default status for all newly created RMAs. This status does not apply to direct returns initiated from a Shipment Order (SO).
Manual Actions:
A
Pending
RMA can be manually updated to
In Transit
or
Cancelled
.
In Transit
What it means:
The return shipment is on its way back to the warehouse.
How it's set:
An RMA can be manually updated from
Pending
to
In Transit
.
Manual Actions:
An
In Transit
RMA can be changed back to
Pending
.
Started
What it means:
The return has arrived at the warehouse and is being processed at the Return Station.
How it's set:
This status is set automatically when the return process begins at the Return Station. It applies to both RMAs and direct SO returns.
Manual Actions:
A
Started
return can be manually updated to
Completed
.
Completed
What it means:
All items in the return have been fully received and processed.
How it's set:
The status automatically changes to
Completed
when all expected items are processed at the Return Station. It can also be manually set from the
Started
status.
Manual Actions:
This is a final status and cannot be changed.
Cancelled
What it means:
The RMA has been cancelled and will no longer be processed.
How it's set:
An RMA can be manually updated from
Pending
to
Cancelled
. This status does not apply to direct SO returns.
Manual Actions:
This is a final status and cannot be changed. A cancelled RMA cannot be processed at the Return Station.
2. Reporting on Completed Returns
Once returns are processed, you can review them in detail using the following reports.
Receiving History Report
This report provides a comprehensive log of all inbound activities, including processed customer returns. It is the best place to see a detailed breakdown of what was received.
How to Use:
Navigate to the
Receiving History
report.
Use the
Filter
option and select a
Receiving Type
of
Return
.
Available Information:
The report will display all return receiving operations, showing key details such as:
The linked RMA and original Shipment Order numbers.
Any notes or damage reasons recorded during processing.
Product images that were uploaded at the Return Station.
Returned Quantities
Returned Warehouse and Location informations.
Transaction History Report
For a high-level audit trail of inventory movements related to returns, use the Transaction History report.
How to Use:
Navigate to the
Transaction History
report.
Use the
Filter
option and select a
Transaction Type
of
Return Receiving
.
Available Information:
This report focuses on the inventory movement itself, showing which products were added back into stock as a result of a return with the related shipment order information.

title: Operational Analytics
content:

Enabling and Accessing the Operational Analytics Module
To provide your team with access to the Operational Analytics module, follow these two main steps: configuring role permissions and managing user licenses via the Add-on screen.

Save your changes.
Once this is done, the Operational Analytics menu item will appear under of the Analytics menu for all users associated with that role.
2. User Authorization and License Management (App Screen)
After the role permissions are set, you must manage the individual user access within the Add-on section:
User Limit:
The Operational Analytics add-on allows authorization for up to 5 users in BETA Phase. You can select and manage these specific users directly from the Operational Analytics card in the App screen.
Summary of Access
Visibility: Controlled via Settings > Role > Analytics.
Seat Allocation: Controlled via the Add-on screen (up to 5 users).
BETA Phase
OPERATIONAL ANALYTICS DASHBOARDS :
INBOUND & INVENTORY DASHBOARD
The
Inbound & Inventory Dashboard
provides a comprehensive view of your warehouse's inventory health, inbound operations, and return activity. Use this dashboard to monitor stock quality, track vendor performance, and identify operational inefficiencies across your fulfillment workflow.
Filter Coverage Guide
Before diving into the tiles, note that filters at the top of the dashboard apply selectively:
Warehouse Code
– Applies to all tiles
except 'Minimum Safety Stock of Products' & 'Item Active / Passive Status By Client'
Client Name
– Applies to all tiles
except
Duration From The Last Completed Count Date To Today.
Expiration Status
– Applies to Damage Reason, Inventory Expiration, and Lot No Tracking.
Vendor Name & Purchase Order Creation Date
– Apply to PO Volume by Type and Avg. Vendor Lead Time.
Return Order Creation Date
– Applies to Return Orders Volume By Client and Return Reason.
Receiving Date
– Applies to Receiving Mix by Pack Type and Receipts Over Time.
1. Dashboard Objective:
1. Dashboard Objective
The Inbound & Inventory Dashboard is designed to give warehouse managers and operations teams full visibility into:
Inventory quality issues
— identifying damaged, missing, or expiring stock before it impacts fulfillment.
Inbound receiving performance
— tracking receipt volumes, pack type breakdowns, and vendor lead times.
Return activity
— understanding which clients generate the most returns and why products are being sent back.
Cycle count accuracy
— measuring how up-to-date and accurate your physical inventory counts are.
Use this dashboard to proactively address stock discrepancies, optimize vendor relationships, and maintain a healthy, accurate inventory.
2. Dashboard Tiles
🔵 Damage Reason Inventory Lines
Provides a breakdown of inventory issues from today's snapshot. It counts unique inventory log records categorized by reasons like
Missing
,
Damaged
, or
Bad Packaging
to help you identify stock loss and improve quality control.
🔵 Inventory Expiration Date Tracking
Tracks product shelf life by looking at inventory log records for items with a recorded expiration date. It compares the
Expiry Date
to today's date, labeling items as
Expired
or
Active
.
🔵 Duration From The Last Completed Count Date To Today
Shows how many days have passed since each location was last counted. It calculates the time difference between the last recorded count date and today.
🔵 Return Orders Volume By Client
Shows the total number of return orders for each client. Use this to identify which accounts have the highest return volumes.
🔵 Return Reason
Categorizes returned items by the reason provided (e.g.,
Failed Delivery
,
Wrong Item
). It counts individual return order lines to help you identify why products are coming back.
🔵 Lot No Tracking
Tracks product batches by looking at your inventory log records. It displays SKUs and their quantities specifically for items that have a Lot number assigned.
🔵 PO Volume by Type
Shows the total number of unique Purchase Orders categorized by their order type (e.g.,
10% Inbound
,
100% Inbound
,
Carton Count
,
FBA Returns
,
Back to Stock
).
🔵 Inventory Missing Quantity By Location
Shows a list of warehouse locations and the total amount of missing stock in each. It calculates the sum of missing quantities from your inventory records.
🔵 Avg. Vendor Lead Time
Measures vendor performance by calculating the average number of days between the
Purchase Order Date
and the
Actual Receiving Date
. This report only includes shipments with a recorded receiving date.
🔵 Receiving Mix by Pack Type
A breakdown of the total quantity received during the selected period, categorized by pack type (e.g.,
Each
,
Carton
,
Irregular
,
Unit
).
🔵 Receipts Over Time
Tracks the monthly trend of total inventory quantities received at your warehouse over the last 12 months.
🔵 Inventory Record Accuracy (IRA) %
Shows the percentage of count tasks where the system quantity matched the physical count quantity exactly (0 variance), broken down by quarter.
🔵 Replenishment vs. Picking Volume
Compares the monthly trend of replenishment activity against picking volume over time.
🔵 Minimum Safety Stock of Products
Products with a minimum safety stock greater than zero, ranked highest to lowest.
🔵 Item Active / Passive Status By Client
Active and passive product counts per client, ranked by active product count from highest to lowest.
​
🔵 Avg. PO Completion Time (Hours) by Month
Displays the average duration (in hours) from PO creation to actual receiving. Includes completed orders only.
​
​
Fulfillment Dashboard
The
Fulfillment Dashboard
provides end-to-end visibility into your outbound operations  from open orders and carrier performance to shipping margins and warehouse job activity. Use this dashboard to monitor order flow, identify bottlenecks, and optimize your fulfillment efficiency.
Filter Coverage Guide
Filters at the top of the dashboard apply selectively across tiles:
Warehouse Code, Client Name & Shipment Order Creation Date
– Applies to all tiles across the dashboard.
Shipment Order Type
– Applies to Open Orders' Type Distribution, Order Distribution, Order Volume By USA States, Order Volume By Status, Shipment Order Urgency Status, Backorder Rate, Orders By Channel, Order Fulfillment Time Idle Orders and
Aging Orders.
Shipment Order Status Code
– Applies to  Order Distribution, Order Volume By USA States, Order Volume by Status, Backorder Rate, Orders By Channel, Job Distribution
Shipment Order Actual Shipment Date
– Applies to Order Distribution, Orders By Carrier, Order Volume By USA States, Monthly Total Shipped Shipment Order Line Volume, Order Volume By Status, Backorder Rate, Daily Label Count, and Shipment Package Usage.
Shipment Line Shipped Date
– Applies to Shipped LP/Box Count By Carrier, Monthly Total Shipped Shipment Order Line Volume, Shipment Package Usage, Daily Label Count, Top 10 Clients by Shipping Volume (Boxes), and Client Based Shipping Margin.
Carrier Label Creation Date
– Applies to Shipped LP/Box Count By Carrier, Shipment Package Usage, Daily Label Count, Top 10 Clients by Shipping Volume (Boxes), and Client Based Shipping Margin.
1. Dashboard Objective
The Fulfillment Dashboard is designed to give warehouse managers and operations teams complete visibility into:
Order pipeline health
— tracking open orders by type, status, and urgency to prevent delays.
Carrier & shipping performance
— monitoring shipped volumes, carrier distribution, and label counts over time.
Warehouse job activity
— identifying idle jobs, pending picks, and multi-item job distribution.
Use this dashboard to keep fulfillment running smoothly, reduce idle work in the warehouse, and make data-driven decisions about carrier strategy and client operations.
2. Dashboard Tiles
🔵 Open Orders' Type Distribution
Displays the volume of active orders categorized by order type (e.g., D2C Order, D2B Order - SPD, D2B Order - LTL/FTL, Sales Order).
🔵 Order Distribution
Provides insights into your order composition by identifying the volume of single vs. multi-item orders.
🔵 Shipped LP/Box Count By Carrier
Tracks the monthly volume of shipped LPs and boxes broken down by carrier (e.g., ShipStation, FedEx, UPS, Stamps.com, EasyPost, Techship, Custom, Partner, RateShops).
🔵 Order Volume By USA States
A geographical heatmap providing insights into order frequency and SKU density across the USA.
🔵 Monthly Total Shipped Shipment Order Line Volume
Monitors your monthly fulfillment momentum by tracking the total shipped shipment order lines over time.
🔵 Orders By Carrier
A comparative view of order volume and SKU quantity per carrier. Displays the distribution of orders across carriers like ShipStation, FedEx, UPS, Stamps.com, EasyPost, Techship, Custom, Partner, and RateShops.
🔵 Shipment Order Urgency Status
Categorizes orders by comparing their Expected Shipment Date to the current date. It identifies
Delayed
orders (date has passed), shipments
Due Today
, and those scheduled for
Tomorrow
or later.
🔵 Order Fulfillment Time
Measures the speed of your operations by calculating the number of days between the
Created Date
and the
Actual Shipment Date
. This report only includes orders with a
Shipped
status and groups them into time tiers (e.g., Same Day, 2 Days).
🔵 Order Volume By Status
Shows order and SKU distribution per order status (e.g., Shipped, Cancelled, ReadyToPick, ReadyToPack, PickingStarted, Open, OnHold, Shortage).
🔵 Shipment Package Usage
Shows the total count of each package type used for shipped orders, broken down by client. Tracks box usage and monitors packaging costs across your operations.
🔵 Orders By Channel
Shows order volume and total SKU quantities categorized by their integration source (e.g., Shopify, Amazon). Orders without a channel assignment are also captured.
🔵 Backorder Rate
Shows the backorder rate across total orders by categorizing shipments by their backorder flag (
Yes
vs.
No
).
🔵 Daily Label Count
Tracks daily warehouse output by counting the unique carrier labels created each day. Provides a day-by-day trend of your shipping volume.
🔵 Job Distribution
Categorizes warehouse activities based on the
Single Item Job
flag within your job type settings. It calculates the total number of unique warehouse jobs and the distinct shipment orders associated with them.
🔵 Idle Job Count
Distribution of unique
Pending
jobs created 2 hours ago, categorized by Job Type. Used to identify and resolve operational bottlenecks.
🔵 Idle Orders – Not Picked
Shows the number of orders and order lines where picking has been planned but hasn't started yet. It counts tasks in
New
status to help you see how much work is waiting in the warehouse.
🔵 Top 10 Clients by Shipping Volume (Boxes)
Ranks your top 10 customers according to their shipped box volume, helping determine the main drivers of your warehouse operations.
🔵 Client Based Shipping Margin
Tracks the profitability of shipping services for each client by comparing raw carrier costs against the total amount billed, revealing the actual shipping margin.
🔵 Aging Orders
Open orders broken down by client, status, and processing age (in days). Excludes shipped, cancelled, on-hold, and ready-to-ship orders. Pivoted by age tier (0–5+ days) to highlight aging orders at a glance.
Management Dashboard
The
Management Dashboard
provides a high-level overview of your warehouse's business performance from client activity and order volumes to shipping costs, carrier performance, and storage utilization. Use this dashboard to monitor operational health and make strategic decisions with confidence.
Filter Coverage Guide
Global Filters (Applies to All Tiles):
Warehouse Code
Client Name
Order Filters:
Actual Shipment Date / Creation Date
— Does not apply to Warehouse Utilization.
1. Dashboard Objective
The Management Dashboard is designed to give senior operations managers and business stakeholders a bird's-eye view of:
Client activity trends
— tracking how many active clients are placing orders over time.
Order volume & revenue
— monitoring the number and total value of created shipment orders.
Carrier performance & costs
— analyzing shipping label response times, label counts, and shipping costs by carrier.
Warehouse capacity
— understanding current storage utilization to plan for growth or identify space inefficiencies.
Order complexity
— measuring average lines per order to anticipate picking effort and labor needs.
Use this dashboard for regular business reviews, capacity planning, and client performance evaluations.
2. Dashboard Tiles
🔵 Number of Active Clients
A monthly count of unique clients placing shipment orders. It visualizes your active customer trend over time to help you assess business expansion and client retention.
🔵 Number of Created Orders
Shows a daily count of unique orders created in the system. By filtering out deleted orders, it visualizes real-time demand trends to help you monitor growth and prepare for high-volume periods based on historical data.
🔵 Total Price of Created Shipment Orders
Shows the monthly total value of all created shipment orders by summing their
Total Price
. It categorizes orders by the month they were created and excludes any cancelled or deleted records.
🔵 Top 20 Sales Products
Displays your top 20 products based on the total quantity of units shipped. It calculates the sum of shipped quantities for all orders in
Shipped
status, grouped by SKU, to help you identify high-demand items and prioritize stock replenishment.
🔵 Number of Created Orders Per Client
Shows the total number of unique shipment orders created for each client. It counts every non-deleted order to help you identify your high-volume accounts and understand which clients drive the most warehouse activity.
🔵 Monthly Average Lines Per Order
Shows the average number of items (lines) in each order per month. It divides the total number of order lines by the unique shipment orders to help you understand order size and warehouse handling complexity.
🔵 Carrier Setup Level Shipping Cost
Displays the total monthly shipping cost broken down by carrier (e.g., ShipStation, FedEx, UPS, Stamps.com, EasyPost, Techship, Custom, Partner, RateShops).
🔵 Total Shipped Box / LP
Shows the total number of physical boxes (License Plates) shipped out each month. It counts unique package IDs for orders that are fully shipped, helping you track your monthly packaging volume and warehouse output.
🔵 Carrier Label Average Response Time
Shows the average response time (in seconds) it takes for each carrier to generate a shipping label.
🔵 Shipping Labels Count By Carrier
Tracks the total number of shipping labels created for each carrier on a monthly basis. Used to monitor outbound packaging volume and labeling density per carrier.
🔵 Average Lines Per Order By Client
Shows the average number of lines (items) per order for each client. It is used to analyze order complexity and the required picking effort in the warehouse.
🔵 Warehouse Utilization
A gauge representing the warehouse occupancy rate based on a daily inventory snapshot. It shows the percentage of storage locations that currently contain stock relative to the total available locations in the warehouse.
🔵 User Warehouse / Client Access Data
Displays active user access permissions by mapping authorized Clients and Warehouses.
🔵 Total Order Weight By Client
Total shipment order weight per client, ranked highest to lowest. Excludes cancelled orders.
Productivity Dashboard
The
Productivity Dashboard
provides a detailed view of your warehouse team's operational performance from hourly picking and packing efficiency to individual associate output, task completion times, and overall facility throughput. Use this dashboard to monitor workforce productivity, identify bottlenecks, and optimize shift planning.
Filter Coverage Guide
Global Filters (Applies to All Tiles):
Warehouse Code, Client Name, Job Type Code
Associate Name (Except: Order Counts By Job Type)
Measurement Date
applies to:
Hourly Picking Efficiency, Hourly Packing Efficiency, Hourly Packed UOM Quantity Per Packer, Hourly Picked UOM Quantity Per Picker, UPH Task Metrics, Facility Output by Process (Volume),Completed Task Units by Shipment Order Type, Order Counts By Job Type and UPH Task Metrics By Warehouse
Task Type Parameter
applies  to:
UPH Task Metrics, Completed Task Units by Shipment Order Type and UPH Task Metrics By Warehouse
1. Dashboard Objective
The Productivity Dashboard is designed to give warehouse managers and operations leads granular visibility into:
Hourly team output
— tracking picking and packing volumes hour by hour to identify peak activity windows.
Individual associate performance
— measuring each team member's daily average output for picking and packing.
Task lead times
— monitoring how long it takes to complete pick, pack, and ship tasks from creation to finish.
Order quality
— evaluating perfect order rates per associate to identify accuracy issues early.
Facility throughput
— understanding total warehouse output across all processes in a single view.
Use this dashboard for daily shift reviews, associate performance evaluations, and continuous improvement initiatives.
2. Dashboard Tiles
🔵 Hourly Picking Efficiency
Tracks the total quantity of items picked each hour for the selected UPH Measurement Date, based on UTC time. It sums up items from completed tasks to show when the warehouse is most active. Each time slot represents the total for that full hour (for example,
16:00
shows all items collected between 16:00 and 17:00).
🔵 Hourly Packing Efficiency
Tracks the total quantity of items packed each hour for the selected UPH Measurement Date, based on UTC time. It sums up items from completed tasks to show when the warehouse is most active. Each time slot represents the total for that full hour (for example,
16:00
shows all items collected between 16:00 and 17:00).
🔵 Hourly Packed UOM Quantity Per Packer
Displays the total quantity of items packed by each team member every hour for the selected UPH Measurement Date, based on UTC time. It breaks down the workload to show individual productivity levels throughout the day. Each time slot represents a 60-minute window (for example,
16:00
shows all items collected between 16:00 and 17:00).
🔵 Hourly Picked UOM Quantity Per Picker
Displays the total quantity of items picked by each team member every hour for the selected UPH Measurement Date, based on UTC time. It breaks down the workload to show individual productivity levels throughout the day. Each time slot represents a 60-minute window.
🔵 Daily Avg. Packed Qty (Last 30 Days)
Displays the average daily quantity of items packed by each team member over a rolling 30-day period. It calculates the mean volume from completed task records to provide a long-term view of individual productivity levels.
🔵 Daily Avg. Picked Qty (Last 30 Days)
Tracks the 30-day average of unique shipment orders picked and completed per person. It divides the total count of distinct orders successfully picked by each team member by 30 to show long-term productivity trends.
🔵 Daily Avg. Packed Orders (Last 30 Days)
Tracks the 30-day average of unique shipment orders packed and completed per person. It divides the total count of distinct orders successfully packed by each team member by 30 to show long-term productivity trends.
🔵 Daily Avg. Picked Orders (Last 30 Days)
Tracks the 30-day average of unique shipment orders completed per person. It divides the total count of distinct orders handled by each team member by 30 to show long-term productivity trends.
🔵 Start to Pack (hr)
Shows the average time in hours it takes to complete a packing task after it has been created over a rolling 3-month period. It measures the duration from
Creation
to
Actual Finish
for all successfully finished tasks each day.
🔵 Start to Pick (hr)
Shows the average time in hours it takes to complete a picking task after it has been created over a rolling 3-month period. It measures the duration from
Creation
to
Actual Finish
for all successfully finished tasks each day.
🔵 Create to Pick (hr)
Shows the average time in hours from when an order is created to when the picking task is finished over a rolling 3-month period. It measures the total lead time for all completed picking tasks each day.
🔵 Create to Pack (hr)
Shows the average time in hours from when an order is created to when the packing task is finished over a rolling 3-month period. It measures the total lead time for all completed packing tasks each day.
🔵 Create to Ship (hr)
Shows the average time in hours from order creation to official shipment over a rolling 3-month period. It measures the complete outbound cycle time for all successfully shipped orders.
🔵 Order Submit to Ship (hr)
Shows the average time in hours from the official Order Date to the Actual Shipment over a rolling 3-month period. It measures the total turnaround time for all shipped orders to help you track end-to-end fulfillment speed and identify periods of heavy backlog.
🔵 Average SKU Count Per Completed Job
Shows the average variety of unique products (SKUs) handled within each completed job over the last 30 days. It measures how many different items are collected in a single job assignment, helping you understand the density of your warehouse jobs.
🔵 Avg Job Completion Duration
Shows the average time in hours spent on each warehouse job from start to finish over the last 30 days. It measures how long a job stays active by calculating the duration between the
Actual Start
and
Actual Finish
timestamps.
🔵 Perfect Order % Per Associate
Calculates the Perfection Rate based on the total order volume processed by each associate. The formula subtracts orders marked as
Missing (Missing Item)
during the picking process from the total order count, displaying the ratio of the remaining
perfect
orders to the total volume.
🔵 UPH Task Metrics
A detailed pivot table showing each associate's total quantity of tasks completed per hour, their Average UPH (Units Per Hour), and Active Hours for the selected UPH Measurement Date and Task Type Parameter.
🔵 Facility Output by Process (Volume)
Tracks the total quantity of items processed across Picking, Packing, and Sorting in hourly intervals. The red line represents the Total Throughput, showing the overall warehouse output. All times are in UTC — for example,
09:00
includes all tasks completed between 09:00 and 10:00.
🔵 Completed Task Units by Shipment Order Type
Total units processed per associate, broken down by shipment order type. Filtered to the selected task type and date.
🔵 Order Counts By Job Type
Order count per job type for the selected date, ranked highest to lowest.
🔵 UPH Task Metrics by Warehouse
Shows each warehouses' daily picking or packing performance (based on the selected filter) broken down by hour (displayed in UTC). For each hour worked, you can see total quantity, average units per hour (UPH), and total active hours. Use this to compare productivity across warehouses and identify peak performance windows throughout the day.
Downloading & Viewing Tile Data
The Operational Analytics dashboards allow you to export data directly from any tile in multiple formats. Below is a guide on how to download tile data and use the drill-down feature where available.
Downloading Data from a Tile
To download data from any tile:
Hover over the tile and click the
three-dot menu (⋮)
in the top-right corner of the tile.
Select
Download data
from the dropdown menu.
Choose your preferred
Format
from the options below.
Click
Download
.
Available download formats:
TXT (tab-separated values)
Excel Spreadsheet (Excel 2007 or later)
CSV
JSON
HTML
Markdown
PNG (Image of Visualization)
Advanced Data Options
When downloading, you can expand the
Advanced data options
section to customize your export:
Results
With visualizations options applied
— Downloads data as it appears in the chart/table view.
As displayed in the data table
— Downloads the raw underlying data table.
Data values
Formatted
— Includes formatting such as number rounding and special characters.
Unformatted
— Raw values with no rounding or special character formatting.
Number of rows to include
Current result table
— Downloads only the rows currently visible.
All results
— Downloads the complete dataset without row limits.
Select this option to ensure you receive the full data export.
Custom
— Allows you to specify a custom number of rows.
Drill-Down & Viewing Underlying Data
Some tiles support a
drill-down
feature, which allows you to click on a bar, slice, or data point within a chart to view the underlying row-level data in a detailed table.
Once the drill-down table opens, you can:
Review the detailed records directly in the modal.
Click the
Download
button in the top-right corner of the modal to export the drill-down data.
📌
Note:
The default data display limit in drill-down tables is
500 rows
. To download the complete dataset beyond this limit, open
Advanced Data Options
in the download dialog and select
All Results
.
📌
Note:
Not every tile has the drill-down feature. It is only available on tiles where the data points are interactive (e.g., bar charts, pie chart slices). If a tile does not support drill-down, clicking on it will not open a detail table.

title: September 2025 - Release Notes
content:
New Feature Highlights
Enable Picker Self-Assign for Mobile Picking Screens
We are pleased to announce a new feature that provides greater control over the job assignment process. A new
'Enable Picker Self-Assign' parameter
has been introduced at the
Job Type
level.
When this setting is active for a given
Job Type
, it enforces a strict one-to-one assignment. This applies to all jobs of that type (including those generated by our
AI Job Optimization
). A picker will initiate an assignment by selecting a job from the pool and accepting a confirmation prompt on their mobile screen.
Once accepted, the job is automatically assigned and locked to them, preventing any other user from selecting it.
(37631, 37637, 37644, 37650, 39006)
Improvement to Wave Rule “Assign to Role” Logic
This release introduces a significant enhancement to the
'Assign to Role' configuration
within
Wave Rules
, addressing a key operational challenge.
Previously, this setting assigned jobs randomly to individual users possessing the selected role. This could result in jobs being allocated to users who were not present, requiring supervisors to manually adjust assignments.
With this update, jobs generated via the
'Assign to Role' method
will no longer be pushed to specific individuals. Instead, they will populate a
role-based job pool
. On the
mobile picking screens
, only users who have been assigned the specified role(s) will have visibility and access to select these jobs. Users without the correct role will not see these jobs, ensuring a clean and targeted workflow for your picking teams. (17481, 17492)
Picking Job Priority Visibility
To help teams focus on the most critical tasks, we've introduced a new
Job Priority
system from configuration through to picking.
View Priority on Mobile
: The
Mobile Picking Job List
now displays the
'Job Priority'
for each job, making urgency clear at a glance.
Sort by Priority
: Users can now sort the job list by
'Job Priority'
to bring the most important tasks to the top of their screen.
Set Priority for AI Waves
: A new
'Job Priority' field
has been added to the
Wave Rule screen
, allowing you to assign a priority level to jobs generated by
AI Waves
.
(39018, 18020, 17978, 19298, 17983)
Transfer Automation Endpoints
This release introduces the
transfer product
and
location/license-plate
endpoints, enabling users to programmatically transfer inventory.
Created a new API endpoint to allow for the transfer of products between locations, improving inventory management flexibility. You can get more details from the original documentation
here.
(39513)
Introduced new API endpoints for transferring inventory by
Location
or
License Plate
, enhancing automation capabilities. You can get more details from the original documentation
here.
(39519)
Enhanced Integration Monitoring Module - Channel Setup Details
Introduced a new
"Channel Setup Details"
dashboard under
Integration Monitoring
, providing summary charts for shipment volumes and success rates, and summary lists of the
“Items for Review”
in a single screen to check and link to the relevant modules.
Enhanced Return Management
Enable Returns to Alternate Warehouses:
Enhancing flexibility for our multi-warehouse users with the new ability to process returns to a different warehouse than the original shipping location. This powerful feature is controlled by a new
"Enable Returns To Alternate Warehouses"
toggle on the
data setup screen
.
When enabled, it allows you to accept returns at any designated warehouse, giving you precise control over your return logistics.
To handle scenarios where the same order number might exist across multiple warehouses, a new dynamic pop-up will now prompt the user to select the correct order, ensuring accuracy.
Prevent Unspecified SKU Returns Functionality:
Return accuracy and control have been improved as the
"Prevent Unspecified SKU Returns"
toggle now functions correctly, giving you the power to block or allow the return of items that were not in the original order.
Return Station - Target Location Capture
To make the process faster for your operators, we have streamlined the workflow at the
Return Station
. The
“Target Location”
is now captured automatically without requiring an extra keystroke, saving time on every return.
For complete details, see our knowledge base article:
Managing Multi-Warehouse Returns
,
Return Process Data Setup
Enhanced Product Attribute Management
We've enhanced product attribute management to give you more flexibility and streamline inventory control. You can now toggle attribute tracking (e.g., Lot Number, Expiry Date) on products with existing stock, eliminating the need to zero out inventory first. (39876,39851)
Here’s a quick overview:
How to Configure
: This feature can be managed from the 'Advanced' tab within the Edit Product screen or through a bulk Excel update.
Open API Product Update method is currently not included in the scope. (PUT/product/update API endpoint)
Key Prerequisite
: To ensure data integrity, this action is only possible if the product has no active warehouse tasks (e.g., picking,count, replenishment) that are not in a "Completed" or "Cancelled" status.
How It Works
: Enabling a new attribute assigns placeholder values (e.g., NEEDS_LOT_UPDATE/2000-01-01) to current stock , which can then be updated using a cycle count or the "Change Attributes" function. Disabling an attribute removes its data from all inventory records.
For complete details, see our knowledge base article:
Enabling and Disabling Attribute Tracking for Products with Existing Inventory
.
Asynchronous API Endpoint for Report Generation
The following endpoints of this new feature will be activated on September 18, 2025.
Introduced new asynchronous API endpoints for requesting bulk exports of entire reports. The process runs in the background to prevent application performance issues.
Users can initiate an export and retrieve the complete file via a secure, temporary URL once it is ready.
This feature is initially available for the
Available to Promise (ATP) report
.
How It Works:
Request Export
: A user sends a
POST
request with the desired report name and filters to initiate the export process.
Check Status
: The system provides a unique identifier by using which users send a
GET
request to check the job's progress.
Download File
: Once the job is complete, the status response will contain a secure, time-limited
downloadUrl
to retrieve the final report file.
For complete details, see our knowledge base article:
Asynchronous Report Export.
What's New/Improved
Added a
'Direct Print Attached Documents' parameter
to the
Client screen
, which allows users to enable or disable the direct printing of documents attached to a
Shipment Order
on the
Packing screen
. (19326, 19310, 19321, 19315)
The user interface for the
Order Inventory Report
has been significantly improved for clarity and detail. To reduce confusion, the columns previously named "Pack Type" and "Product Qty" have been renamed to
"UOM Pack Type"
and
"Allocated UOM Qty"
respectively. Furthermore, new columns have been added to the report, including the inventory's actual
"Pack Type"
and
"Allocated Pack Qty"
, as well as
"Production Date"
,
"PO Number"
,
"Receiving Date"
, and detailed LPN dimension and weight information. (38484, 38495)
The mobile
Sorting screen
has been updated to ensure the directed
Cell Location
remains visible at all times, even on small-screen devices. (41041)
Added a
'Disable Electronic Trade Document Submission' toggle
to the
FedEx carrier setup
, providing users with the option to manage international customs documentation manually. (39603)
Improved the reliability of the address verification process by introducing an automatic retry mechanism, which prevents orders from getting stuck during temporary service outages. (39446)
Enhanced the handling of multi-package shipments for
UPS SurePost
and
FedEx SmartPost
services by processing each package individually for accurate rate retrieval and label generation. (38518)
Updated the
FedEx integration
to correctly map the incoterm value from DDU to DDP for international shipments billed to a third party. (41440)
Added change log tracking for third-party billing fields on shipment orders, ensuring all updates are logged in the change log. (40238)
You can now see the carrier’s
expected delivery date
on
Shipment Orders
, reports, exports, and APIs for more accurate delivery tracking. (38224, 38230)
Improved the item import and update Excel templates by adding the
'Hazmat Class Division'
field and correcting the
'Hazmat ID'
field name. (40041)
Easypost international shipments
now include each item’s SKU in the
customs_items
object, ensuring accurate and detailed customs declarations. (41434)
Easypost integration has 3 new shipping method  for Veho carrier we have
premiumEconomy, groundPlus
and for UPSDAP carrier we have new method called
UPSGroundsaverGreaterThan1lb
(41638)
Custom carrier integrations
now capture the expected delivery date from the carrier’s API response and populate it in the
Carrier Shipment Details report
. (38218)
Optimized the custom carrier integration by adding the
warehouse code
to rate and label requests, reducing the need for extra API calls. (40809)
When printing labels for multiple identical orders at once, all labels in
ZPL format
are now merged into a single file. (40358)
Enhanced the
Transaction History report API endpoint
to include and allow filtering by
workOrderCode
, providing more granular analysis for work order-related transactions. (41094)
The
GET Location List API endpoint
now supports filtering by
locationBarcode
for more precise location data retrieval. (41094)
Added a new validation to prevent the
'Cancel Picking' action
from the Logiwa Screens for orders that have already been allocated to a robotics job, ensuring data consistency. (41100)
Performance Improvements
Optimized the
"Available to Promise"
inventory query to improve performance and reliability. This change resulted in a 35.37% reduction in average response time for this high-volume request. (39268)
The
Total Inventory report
query has been optimized to consume significantly fewer system resources, improving overall application stability. (39183)
Improved the performance of the
Work Order Create Kit
functionality, reducing processing time for both validation and saving.
The response time for source location validation has been reduced by over 97.4%, and the final save action is now over 92.3% faster. (40221)
What's Fixed
Fixed an issue where the warehouse name in the
'Ship From' address
within
Carrier Setup
was not displaying correctly on the
Create Label screen
. (37236)
Removed deleted and inactive shipping services from the
"Shipping Service" filter
on the
Shipment Order screen
. (39036)
Improved the error message on the
Create Shipment Order API
for the
GiftNote
field to clarify the 250-character limit. (38238)
Fixed an issue where voiding a manually entered tracking number did not remove it from all associated shipment orders. (40850)
Corrected an issue in the
Custom Carrier integration
where void requests were sending the carrier and shipping option names instead of their required codes. (40815)
Fixed a bug on the mobile
shipment plan screen
where a partially shipped order was incorrectly marked as "Shipped". (41117)
Fixed an issue where the
Change Log
for an allocation cancellation displayed an incorrect user. (34848)
Corrected the total count on the warehouse job list, fixing the pagination failure in the
'Merge into Existing Job' tab
. (38490)
Fixed a bug preventing the removal of a retailer from a shipment order. (38598)
Fixed an issue where canceled tasks were causing duplicate entries on the
Packing Slip report
. (39323)
Added the
OrderCode
and
ShipmentOrderCode
fields to the
BOL
and
Shipment Report
data views. (39563)
Implemented validation to prevent non-GUID values from being saved in GUID fields for
Job Type
conditions. (40559)
Resolved an issue where the 'Exclude' filter option in
Job Types
was incorrectly excluding orders with null values. (35820)
Fixed an issue where the status of a partially shipped order was incorrectly displayed on the shipment plan. (40678)
Resolved an error where the
Bill of Lading (BOL)
quantity was incorrect for orders assigned to the same picking job. (40885)
Corrected an issue in the
Bill of Lading (BOL) report
where customer information was not being displayed correctly. (41187)
Fixed an issue where the replenishment wave rule would fail if the "Area Type" condition was set to "Is Empty". (34639)
Added the "Location Barcode", "Rack", and "Position" columns to the
Location Screen's Excel export
. (34696)
Resolved an issue where the
"isUseItemsOwnBoxForShipping"
parameter was not updating on the UI when set via the API. (38281)
Fixed a bug in the dynamic replenishment process to ensure that the walking path priority is correctly applied when suggesting replenishment locations. (33970)
Fixed a bug that prevented the creation of
LP Numbers
with special characters through the UI. (36141)
Removed the Min/Max Volume and Replenishment Threshold fields from Excel imports and corrected the Min QTY display on the
Location Screen
. (28993)
The "Digital" toggle can now be updated during a product edit using the Excel import. (20150)
Enhanced the
Kit Inventory Report
to include all kit items, even those with insufficient components. (24098)
Added validation to the
Kit Product Excel import
to prevent duplicate component entries. (24243)
Fixed an issue where component products with zero inventory were not being listed in the
Kit Component Inventory Report
. (27550)
Corrected an issue where SKUs with a date-like format were incorrectly converted to dates in the
Inventory by Location Excel export
. (29051)
Resolved an error that occurred during
Work Order
allocation cancellation on the
Jobs screen
. (29573)
Fixed an internal server error that occurred when creating a
Purchase Order
with a null SKU via the API, even when "Allow Creation without Product" was enabled. (29655)
Improved the error handling for duplicate rows during inventory import to prevent data inconsistencies. (30071)
Fixed an issue where UPC/Barcode values with leading or trailing spaces were saved incorrectly, causing scan mismatches. (35991)
Fixed an issue where the 'Received Quantity' field was blank in the
Purchase Order details Excel export
. (36253)
Fixed the
LP Number Excel import
to correctly apply default physical attributes from the LP Type. (37972)
Resolved an issue where the
Dynamic Replenishment Report
showed multiplied quantities for users with access to multiple warehouses. (40723)
Updated the system to enforce
serial number
uniqueness per SKU rather than globally, allowing the same serial number to be used for different products within the same order. (40233)
Clear error message now shows if duplicate UPCs are detected when “
Allow Unique SKU Barcodes
” is enabled. (31375)
Fixed an issue with the
LP Number Excel import
that incorrectly prevented the use of duplicate codes across different warehouses. (40734)
Corrected the product excel import process to properly handle special characters in the
Lot/Batch Regex

title: Create a Job Type for Work Orders
content:
It's necessary to create a job type for work orders to create kit-to-stock products. This article will walk you through the process.
Step-by-Step Guide
Navigate to the
Job Types
page.
If you have trouble finding the screen, please use the
Search Option
on the menu bar.
Click on
Create New Job Type
in the upper right corner.
Select the
Work Order
Operation Type
from the available options.
Proceed to the
General
screen.
General
Enter values for the required fields. Explanations for the fields are below.
Field
Description
Name*
Type the name for this job type.
Required field.
Warehouse*
Select the warehouse using this job type.
Required field.
Operation Type
Selected on the previous screen. Cannot be edited here.
Allocation Algorithm*
Select an existing allocation algorithm.
Required field.
Notes:
The system will use the
Inventory Conditions
and
Group By
for the allocation algorithm you select, but will disregard the
Order Conditions
.
Select an algorithm that will allocate each kit component and does not use hierarchical pack types, as only UOM components are supported at this time.
Description
Type a longer name/description for this job type.
Once you've filled in the required fields, click
Next
.
Settings
From this tab, you'll set the necessary parameters for the job you're creating.
You can choose to enable or disable
Override for Last Job:
When enabled, if you define a batch size for this job using the
Batch Size
limitation method
and the number of remaining orders is less than the minimum quantity, the remaining orders will be added to the last job.
The
Picking & Kitting
parameter cannot currently be changed here.
The next setting in this section is
Batch Size
.
Select the allowed batch size from the dropdown. You can choose
Number of Items
or
Number of Orders.
Using
Min
and
Max
, define the minimum and maximum number of orders/items for the batch.
For example, consider a job type with a maximum
N of Different SKU
of 12 and a maximum
N of Item
of 25. Jobs using this job type will be created so that up to 12 different items can be picked at the same time, and the sum of the same items can be up to 25.
This is
not
a required field.
Next, select the
Mobile Screen Type
that will use this job type. You can currently choose to use the
Pick to Location
screen or not.
After adding the necessary information, click
Next
to move to the
Advanced
tab.
Advanced
In this section, you can add some conditions for the work orders, including information like the client or work order type. These are optional, but can help you further customize this job type.
To add a condition, click
Add Filter
and select the
Plus (+)
next to the filter you wish to add.
To complete job type creation, click
Save
.
You can now use this job type when creating work orders.

title: Create a Count Plan
content:
Overview
To ensure inventory accuracy, warehouse managers must perform regular inventory counts. A Count Plan is the first step in this process, outlining which items or locations will be audited. This guide will walk you through the methods for creating a count plan in Logiwa IO.
Methods for Creating a Count Plan
You can create a count plan using one of two methods, depending on your needs:
Manual Creation:
This method is ideal for creating a single count plan with specific locations or SKUs directly within the Logiwa IO interface. The steps for this process are detailed below.
Bulk Import via Excel:
This method is best for creating multiple count plans at once or for building a large, complex count plan with a high volume of locations or SKUs. For detailed instructions on this method, please see our guide:
Import Count Plan via Excel File
Manual Creation Process
Step 1: Navigate to Count Plans
To begin, navigate to the
Count Plans
screen. If you have trouble locating this screen, please use the main search bar.
Step 2: Define General Information
Click
Create New Count
in the upper-righthand corner of the screen.
Fill in the required fields in the pop-up window.
Field
Description
Name*
A unique name for your count plan.
Required field.
Warehouse*
The warehouse where the count will take place.
Required field.
Description
An optional field for more details about the count plan.
Scheduled Count Date*
The date for which the count is scheduled.
Required field
.
Lock Locations
This parameter determines how the system handles inventory transactions for locations included in the count.
Lock Locations Parameter
Enabled:
All locations in the count plan are locked as soon as the count job is created and remain locked until the entire count plan is completed and approved. This is the best option for ensuring the highest accuracy, especially for high-value or fast-moving items, as it prevents any inventory changes from occurring during the count.
Disabled:
A location is only locked while the counter is actively counting it. Once the count for that specific location is submitted, it becomes available for other operations. This option provides more operational flexibility.
Step 3: Add Count Tasks
After defining the general information, click
Next
to move to the Tasks section. You must choose to create your plan by either
Location
or
SKU
; they cannot be mixed in the same plan.
To create a Location-based count:
Ensure the
Location
tab is selected.
Click the
Add
button.
In the pop-up, search for and select the checkbox next to each location you wish to include in the count.
Click
Add Selected Locations
.
To create a SKU-based count:
Select the
SKU
tab.
Click the
Add
button.
In the pop-up, search for and select the checkbox next to each SKU you wish to include in the count.
Click
Add Selected Products
.
Step 4: Save the Plan
Once you have added all the necessary locations or SKUs, click the
Save
button to finalize the count plan. You can now view your new plan on the
Count Plans
screen.
Important Considerations During Creation
Inventory Status Restriction:
You cannot include locations or SKUs in a count plan if they contain inventory that is already part of an active outbound process (i.e., has a status of Picked, Packed, Sorted, or Loaded).
Location Counts:
If a location contains such inventory, the count task will be created with a "Cancelled" status to prevent data conflicts. A note will appear in the count plan details explaining the reason.
SKU Counts:
The system will not create a count task for an SKU that has inventory in these statuses.
What's Next?
Once your count plan has been created, the next step is to generate a count job. A job contains the specific tasks that your warehouse staff will execute on their mobile devices. You can create a job in two ways:
Manually:
From the
Count Plans
screen, select your plan and use the "Create Job" button. You will need to have a
Count Job Type
configured.
To learn how to configure a job type for cycle counts, read our guide:
Create a Job Type for a Cycle Count
.
Automatically:
For recurring counts, you can automate job creation by setting up a
Cycle Count Wave Rule
.
To learn more, read our guide:
Create Wave Rules for a Cycle Count
.

title: Pack Types, Product Types, and Product Groups
content:
Need to know more about the differences between pack types, product types, and product groups? Product-related categories can be viewed and modified in the
Data Setup
section under
Settings
. Click below to learn about each one.
Pack Types
There are two types of pack types under the pack type umbrella in the system, UOM and parent pack types. Any pack types you create can be assigned as UOM or parent pack types. To learn more about the difference between these pack types, please
visit this article
.
You are required to include the UOM pack type when setting up your products. The default pack type is
Unit
, but additional pack types are easy to add. Just follow the steps below.
Navigate to the
Data Setup
page and click
Pack Types
from the left sidebar.
Click the
Create New Product Pack Type
button on the right side of the screen.
A sidebar will open. Enter the new pack type in the
Product Pack Type
field. You can add any name that makes sense for the products in your warehouse.
Hit the
Save
button.
A confirmation message will appear at the bottom of the screen, and your new pack type will display in the list.
To
Edit
or
Delete
a pack type, simply click the
3 Dots
menu next to that product type and select the option you need.
Product Types
Product types are optional conditions you can apply to your products to help categorize them. Your account will include a number of defaults, but you can add more at any time following these steps.
To begin, navigate to the
Data Setup
screen.
Click
Product Type
to load this section.
Click the
Create New Product Type
button.
A sidebar will open. Enter the new product type in the
Product Type
field. You can add any name that makes sense for the types of products in your warehouse.
Click
Save
.
If the product type was created successfully, a confirmation message will display.
To
Edit
or
Delete
a product type, simply click the
3 Dots
menu next to that product type and select the option you need.
Product Groups
Product groups are optional, broader groups than product types that can be used as additional categories to track your products. Unlike pack types and product types, there are no system defaults for product groups. If you wish to add some, follow the steps below.
Navigate to the
Data Setup
screen.
Click
Product Group
on the left sidebar.
Click the
Create New Product Group
button.
A sidebar will open. Enter the new product type in the
Product Group
field. You can add any name that makes sense for the types of products in your warehouse.
Click
Save
.
If the product group was created successfully, a confirmation message will display.
To
Edit
or
Delete
a product group, simply click the
3 Dots
menu next to that product type and select the option you need.

title: Import Products via Excel File
content:
In a bustling warehouse, you may need to add numerous products simultaneously. Fortunately, Logiwa makes this process simple. Not only can you create locations individually, but you can also import your product locations in bulk, which saves you a considerable amount of time. This article will show you how.
Step-by-Step Guide
To begin, navigate to the
Products
screen.
The
Import
button is on the right hand side of the screen. Click this button and select
Bulk Import Products
.
You are now on the
Bulk Import Products
page. If you need to, download the Excel template file via the
Download
button.
Open the template. You will see some sample data to give you an idea of how to fill out the file. Please make sure to delete this data before uploading it.
File preparation guidelines/information:
This import document can be used to create new products.
Green-colored fields are required and cannot be left blank; gray-colored fields are optional and can be filled only when needed.
Do not alter the names of the columns, as the columns' distinct headers enable the system to match the Excel data with Logiwa's fields.
All fields are broadly explained in the
Field Description
sheet.
The
Glossary
sheet contains information about countries and some of the list values.
This sheet cannot be used to update existing products.
The first line in the template is an example product. Please delete this row before starting the import.
When the file is imported, please wait a few seconds, then click on the
Refresh List
button to see the results of your import.
Click the
3-Dot
icon to see the import details. You can view lines that failed to import along with the failure reason.
​
Fill in the template according to these requirements and save it.
Once it's ready, upload the Excel file from the
Bulk Import Products
screen. You can either drag and drop your file into the blank space in the center or select
Browse
to find the file from local storage.
After you select the file, you should see it listed under file icon. Click the
Upload
button to continue.
After the file uploads your products, another screen will load with the information you've imported. This is an opportunity to make sure your data matches with the fields in Logiwa.
The
Matched
column will display a green check if
Logiwa Fields
and
File Column Headers
match for each column. Otherwise, a red X will indicate a mismatch.
The
Preview Data
column shows the initial 3 rows of your data as a sample.
If there is a mismatch between Logiwa and the excel file's columns, you can select which Logiwa field corresponds to your file's column by pressing
Choose Field
and then selecting from the dropdown menu.
As long as the field has not already been used, it can be selected.
Once an unused Logiwa field is selected, the
Matched
column will change to a check mark.
Make sure each section is matched to a Logiwa field, then press the
Import
button
in the bottom right corner
to finalize the process.
You will be directed to the upload screen and a message will show that your import was completed.
You can now check the status of your import. The bottom of the screen will display the history of your imports with the following information:
Status:
This will say if your import was
Successful
or
Failed
Row Count:
This names how many rows were in your import.
Success Count:
Count of successfully imported rows
Error count:
Count of rows that were not imported due to errors
Uploaded By:
User that uploaded the data
Creation Date:
The date and time the file was uploaded
You can also click the
Actions
menu to access links to
Details
or
Download Original File
.
Selecting
Details
will take you to a sidebar that summarizes the upload with more information. If you had errors, this will give more information on the issue.

Help Center
to search more documents!

title: Billing for Kit-to-Order Products
content:
When processing Kit-to-Order shipments, you can charge separately for the virtual kit (the assembly service) and each component within the kit. Logiwa IO supports billing for Kit-to-Order fulfillment, providing precise control over how kitting services and their physical components are charged.
Charge-By Options for Kit-to-Order Products
There are two dedicated
Charge By
options for shipments containing Kit-to-Order products, available when configuring a Billing Fee Card with
Operation Type: Shipment
.
Per Kit Item
Charges a fee based on the number of Kit-to-Order SKUs (parent items) shipped within the order.
Pricing Model
How It Works
Per Unit
A fixed price per parent kit SKU shipped
From To
Different rates for the first kit vs. additional kits (e.g., 1st kit @ $2.50, additional @ $1.25)
Tier Based
Rate changes based on total kit quantity in the order (e.g., 1–3 kits @ $1.50 each, 4+ @ $1 each)
Per Component
Charges a fee based on the number of individual components of each Kit-to-Order SKU within the order.
Pricing Model
How It Works
Per Unit
A fixed price per component item inside each kit shipped
From To
Different rates for first vs. additional components per kit (e.g., 1st component @ $2.00, each additional @ $0.50)
Tier Based
Rate changes based on total component count within a single kit SKU (e.g., 1–3 components @ $1.00 each, 4–6 @ $1.25 each, 7+ @ $1.50 each)
💡 Kit-to-order billing applies only to items where the product is classified as a Kit-to-Order type. Standard SKUs and Kit-to-Stock products are excluded from these calculations automatically.
Excluding Kit-to-Order Components from Standard Fee Cards
When you apply both a
Per Component
fee and a standard
Per Product
fee to the same shipment, component items would otherwise get charged twice. The "
Order Contains Kit-to-Order SKU"
condition prevents this.
Step-by-Step: Configure the Exclusion Condition
Navigate to
3PL Billing
and open the relevant contract to find the related
Fee Card
.
Select the Fee Card where
both
the
Fee By
and
the Charge By
are set to
Per Product
(Shipment operation type).
In the
Condition
section, locate the condition labeled
Order Contains Kit-to-Order SKU
.
Under
Apply Fee to
, select one of the following:
Exclude Kit Components
— The fee card will skip any items that are components of a Kit-to-Order SKU in the order
All Items
— The fee card charges all items, including the Kit-to-Order components (default behavior)
Click
Save
.
If you select
Exclude Kit Components
, the billing engine will skip component-level items for Kit-to-Order SKUs when calculating this fee card.
If the order contains a mix of standard SKUs and Kit-to-Order components, standard SKUs are still charged normally.
