title: Create a Purchase Order
content:
Do you need to increase your inventory by placing orders with your vendors? This article will guide you through the simple process of creating purchase orders in Logiwa, so you can get your products and track orders without a hitch.
Step-by-Step Guide
First, navigate to the
Purchase Orders
screen.
If you cannot find the screen, please use the
Search Option
on the menu bar.
Click the
Create Purchase Order
button.
You'll now go through a 5-step process to create your purchase order.
PO Details
In the
PO Details
tab, you'll need to fill in the required fields, marked with an asterisk (*).  Click to expand the section below to view explanations for these fields.
PO Details Fields
Warehouse*: Required.
Select the warehouse this purchase order is for.
Client*:
Required.
Select the client this purchase order will be created for.
PO Number*: Required.
Enter a unique purchase order code (by client), max 50 characters.
PO Type*: Required.
Select the category for your purchase orders based on pre-defined types
(learn more about creating these here
). For each purchase order type, specific attributes can be assigned to further customize and streamline the ordering process.
PO Date*: Automatically filled by the system, required.
Refers to the date and time the purchase order was started.
Planned Receiving Date:
Select the date and time the purchase order is expected to be received.
Actual Receiving Date:
Select the actual date and time the purchase order was received. Can be updated after this initial process.
Planned Arrival Date:
Select the date and time the purchase order is expected to arrive.
Actual Arrival Date:
Select the actual date and time the purchase order was arrived. Can be updated after this initial process.
Reference Number:
If you have another specific code, such as the original
Order Code
provided by your vendor or other sources, you can enter them in this field. Purchase orders can be searched by this number.
Note:
Field for any additional notes needed for this purchase order, max 500 characters.
After you fill the necessary fields, click the
Next Step
button.
Products
In the
Products
tab, you will add the products being purchased. You cannot proceed without adding products.
To learn more about creating purchase order types,
see this article
.
The functions that you can fulfill in this section are listed below:
Add SKUs to your purchase order
Search for SKUs, Product Names, or Barcodes (UPC) to locate existing products.
Edit an added product
Delete an added product
Create a new product that does not already exist in the system
Monitor the total number of products in the purchase order
Download all the SKUs within the purchase order in an Excel file
Create labels
See total quantity
To access these features, either enter the SKU to find the product you wish to locate or click the
Create New Product
button.
Regarding kit products,
Kit-to-Stock
products can be added to Purchase Orders & can be received as usual.
Kit-to-Order
products
cannot
be received through purchase orders, neither on web nor in the mobile app.
In case it is necessary to include
kit-to-order
products to purchase orders, please proceed by including kit's components in purchase orders.
You can also add some extra information to the each line within a purchase order, either when adding a SKU or by selecting that SKU and choosing the
Edit
option. Fields marked with an asterisk (*) are required.
From this sidebar, you can add/change:
Pack Type:
Predefined unit name used to track for this product (unit, box, piece, etc.). Learn more about adding pack types
here
.
Quantity*:
Total number of the product being purchased
Price Per Pack Type*:
Given price for each pack type, used to calculate
Total Price
, which cannot be edited manually.
Received Quantity:
Total number of product received.
Receiving Location:
Where a product will be received to.
Expiry Date:
Expiry date of a product being received.
Lot Batch Number:
Lot batch number of a product being received.
LP Type:
Predefined LP type that the product will be received to.
LP Number:
LP number that the product will be received to.
After you are done with adding this information, select
Apply
to save your changes.
After creating your purchase order, you can review the purchase order and download all the SKUs within the purchase order in an Excel file using the
Export
button.
Once you've added all the products that are necessary, you can proceed by clicking the
Next Step
button.
Vendor
From the
Vendor
tab, you can fulfill the following functions:
Choose the vendor that will fulfill the purchase order.
Create a new vendor that does not exist in the system.
Vendors you have already added to the system will be displayed on this screen. You can select them by checking the box next to the
Vendor Display Name
.
To add a new vendor, select the
Add New Vendor
option and fill in the required information. To edit an existing vendor, select the
Edit
button next to the vendor's name.
After you are done with
Vendor
section, proceed by clicking the
Next Step
button.
Other Info
In the
Other Info
section, you can add
custom fields, which are dynamic fields that you can
learn more about here.
To add a custom field, select the
Add/Edit Custom Field
button and fill in the required information in the
Create Custom Field
sidebar.
Proceed to the final section by clicking the
Next Step
button.
Confirm
In the
Confirm
section, a summary of your purchase order data will be available for your review. If you notice something that needs to be updated, click the
Back
button at the bottom left to return to the relevant section.
You can finalize your purchase order by clicking
Confirm Purchase Order
.
Purchase Order Statuses
It is important to understand the statuses of a purchase order in order to properly manage them. Below are descriptions of the statuses including when they are used in the system and when they may change from one to another.
Pending
The purchase order has been created, and no action has been taken afterwards, such as receiving any item within it.
Started
The items within the purchase order have arrived in the warehouse and some of them have begun to be received.
Completed
All the items within the purchase order have been received.
Cancelled
Purchase orders can be cancelled due to mistakes during creation, incorrect ordering, etc.
Only orders with a pending status can be cancelled, and once a purchase order is cancelled, it cannot be reversed. Learn more about
canceling purchase orders here
.

title: Skip during Picking (Mobile)
content:
During picking, there might be some situations that slows down/stops the picking process, such as having another picker picking products from that same location, or perhaps the location itself not being physically accessible at that moment. In case you encounter such scenarios, there is an option to Skip the task in Logiwa.
Pick to Location
Click on three dots and select "Skip and Pick Last" button
Once operation is completed, the picking screen will show the next picking task. The skipped task will be shown once all other picking tasks in this job are completed.
Pick and Sort
Click Three Dots button in Location Confirmation screen and select "Skip and Pick Last" button
Once operation is completed, all tasks for this location will be skipped. Location Confirmation screen will show the next location that will be visited. The skipped tasks will be shown once all other picking tasks in this job are completed.

title: Create a Billing Contract
content:
This article offers a step-by-step guide on creating a billing form that will produce a billing report that can be used to create invoices for 3PL clients. With our Billing function, you can reduce confusion regarding billing and enhance transparency in financial transactions with 3PL clients. Clear billing terms and detailed service descriptions also play an important role in establishing trust and ensuring prompt payments. Read below to learn more about creating a billing form for your clients.
Step-by-Step Guide
First, navigate to the
Billing
section of Logiwa IO.
Please use our search bar to easily locate this section.
Select
Create Billing
from the right hand side of the screen. You can also edit and delete previously created billing forms from this screen.
Billing
Fill in the necessary details in the
Billing Form
section. Each field is required, and explained below the screenshot.
Field
Description
Billing Form Name*
Refers to the name of the billing form being used to document and process financial transactions. Will be viewable by the client.
Client*
The organization for whom the billed services are being provided, and who will be responsible for payment of the billed amounts. Each contract can only be set to one client at a time. Choose from your list of available clients.
Warehouse*
The warehouse using this billing arrangement. Billing contracts are client- and warehouse-based. Choose from your list of available warehouses for the client you chose.
Calc. Start Date*
The specific date from which billing calculations will begin. It marks the starting point for determining billing frequency.
Billing Frequency*
Billing frequency is the length of time between two billing invoices, beginning from the
Calc. Start Date
. The current periods available within Logiwa are as follows:
Monthly
Weekly
Daily
Bi-weekly
Bi-Monthly
Semi-Monthly
Once you've filled in all feels, click
Save
to continue.
Fees
The next step is adding fees. These will determine what you'll charge your client for, as well as under what conditions.
See this article for a complete list of the available operations, billing fees, charges, and conditions available in Logiwa.
Click
Create New
to proceed.
To add a fee, begin by selecting the operation type you'll use for this fee. Some examples include Receiving, Storage, Pick and Pack, Shipment, and VAS etc.
Add the
Fee Name
, which will be displayed on the contract line.
You can now select the
Fee By
and/or
Fee Calculation Type if available for the selected operation.
Currently,
Fee Calculation Type
is only use for
Storage
operations.
Fee By
is used for
Shipment, Pick & Pack, Receiving, Storage, Return and Work Order
operation types.
You can add a condition at this time, or move directly to setting the charge for the current line. Adding conditions is optional, so it is described separately
in this section
.
Setting Minimum and Maximum Prices
You can set a price floor (minimum) and ceiling (maximum) for calculated fees to ensure charges remain within a specific range. This feature is available for
Receiving
,
Pick & Put
,
Shipment
,
Return
,
Work Order
,
VAS
, and
Storage
fees.
Use Minimum Price
: Toggle to
Yes
to enable this setting. The
Minimum Price
field will become editable. If the calculated fee is less than this value, the system will apply the minimum price.
Use Maximum Price
: Toggle to
Yes
to enable this setting. The
Maximum Price
field will become editable. If the calculated fee exceeds this value, the system will apply the maximum price.
Charges
Next, you'll use the
Add Charge
section to add the amount that will be charged for this part of the contract. This is a non-optional part of the setup process.
The
Charge By
options will vary depending on the selection made in the
Fee By
field.
See this section for a list of charges.
Examples of potential selections are pictured below.
Once you've set at least one charge for this contract line, click the
Save
button to add it to your billing form.
After it saves, you'll be able to review your added contract lines in the
Summary
section on the right side of the screen.
Add Condition
To add conditions that will limit the triggering of this fee, simply click on
Plus (+)
icon next to the
Add Condition
text.
This action will open the
Add Condition
pop-up. You can now select conditions (
Charge If
), which will change your available
Comparator
options.
For example if you choose to charge by
Product Weight
, you can choose from
Comparators
related to amounts, such as is, greater than, less than, and between.
In this example, the fee will only be charged for products weighing between 5 and 10 kilograms. The unit is determined by your warehouse's default weight unit.
Click
Save
to complete this contract line one you are satisfied with the results.

title: 08/14/2023 Release Notes
content:
This release requires the mobile app update, as well. Please update the Logiwa mobile app after the release to start using the updated version.
What's New/Improved
A new action has been added to Putaway Algorithm with the purpose of suggesting a reasonable location based on the
product group & location zone match
that can be set in the redesigned location zone screen.
Filter functionality has been added to the
Users
screen.
A new UI design has been implemented on the
Printouts & Labels
screen.
Custom declaration and custom fields are added for kit products.
Each workflow with the
Update
trigger now only updates a shipment order
once
. I.e, if a shipment order is updated by a specific workflow once, the shipment order will not be updated by the same workflow once again.
Customer phone number, address line 1 (billing), address line 2 (billing), postal code (billing), city (billing), country (billing), and state (billing)
fields can be set as a workflow condition.
Store Update Notes
,
Is Store Updated,
and
Store Order Number
fields can be set as a workflow condition.
For each carrier integration setup,
markup rates
can be set up on either a percentage or fixed rate basis. These markup rates will be applied to the carrier rate while generating the carrier labels from carriers.
Shipment Order Tags
have been added to the
Packing Station
screen.
Transaction User
field has been added to the
Transaction History
filters.
The user’s time zone information has been added to the
Preferences
screen as a Read-Only field which is retrieved from Computer’s Time Zone setup
What's Fixed
A user seeing all the data belonging to all the warehouses in the system regardless of authorization has been prevented.
Incorrect projection of several parameters in the Purchase Order screen that used to mislead the users such as Received Quantity, Total Price, etc. has been fixed.
Some UI-related bugs in the putaway screen have been fixed.
Excel export function is now available so that the users can download all the PO lines on a purchase order basis.
The empty & not empty comparator issue in workflows has been fixed.
A minor glitch in the shipment order edit has been fixed. (if the shipment order has a label). Shipment orders can be edited if a label is assigned to them already, except the customer information in the shipment order which will not be editable if any label is present.
An issue with workflow condition group operators has been fixed.
A small issue with UPS label message selection is fixed.
A minor glitch in the carrier selection dropdown in the Packing Screen has been fixed.
There was an issue in the Next Run Date column in the Wave Rule Set screen because of the user’s time zone. This issue has been fixed.
Scanning a cell location or entering LP’s location as a cell location is prevented in the Pick to Location screen. This was causing issues in Pick and Sort operations.
A new shipment exception type has been added to the Shipment by Location screen which checks whether the order has a shipping label or not.
API/Webhooks
The
actionIdentifier
parameter has been added to the
GET Transaction History
API
A new webhook called
Order Shipment
has been developed

title: Update a Custom Field
content:
Once you have
created a customized field

title: Using "Item's Own Box" for Shipping on the Packing Screen
content:
Overview
Logiwa IO introduces a feature to handle products that are shipped in their own boxes rather than using standard shipment package types.
This feature allows users to configure products to be packed in their own boxes and eliminates the need to manually select a Shipment Package Type during the packing process.
This functionality is activated through a toggle on the Product screen and simplifies the packing process for certain products.
"Item's Own Box" Shipment Package Type
A default
Shipment Package Type
named
"Item's Own Box"
is automatically created on the backend for each warehouse.
This package type is distinguished from other Shipment Package Types with a special flag and cannot be seen in the Shipment Packages grid or in Package Type dropdown lists.
"Item's Own Box" package type is only used
on the Packing screen
when a product with the
Use Item's Own Box for Shipping
toggle enabled is scanned.
Product Configuration
On the
Product screen
, under the
Pack Type settings
, there is a toggle called
Use Item's Own Box for Shipping
.
When this toggle is enabled, the user is required to enter the
Length
,
Width
,
Height
, and
Weight
of the product for correct product configuration.
Enabling this toggle signals to the packing process that the product will be packed in its own box, and the user will not need to select a Shipment Package Type on the Packing screen.
Packing Screen General Rules
Shipment Package Type: "Item's Own Box"
package type will not appear in the Shipment Package Type dropdown unless a product is setup as
Use Item's Own Box for Shipping: TRUE
is scanned.
Icon Display:
If the product is setup as
Use Item's Own Box for Shipping: TRUE
, an icon will appear next to the product on the Packing screen to indicate it will be shipped in its own box.
Pack All & Line-Based Pack Restrictions:
If any product in the order has
Use Item's Own Box for Shipping
enabled, the user will not be able to use the "Pack All" until all products with this setting are packed individually.
If any product in the order has Use Item's Own Box for Shipping enabled, the packer will not be able to pack multiple quantities for that product by using line-based "Pack" button.
Scenarios on the Packing Screen
Scenario 1: Single Item Order with "Item with Box" enabled
Once the product is scanned:
Shipment Package Type
will automatically be set to
"Item's Own Box"
.
Length, Width, Height, and Weight
fields will be populated based on the product's configured dimensions and weight.
Shipment Package Type
dropdown will be grayed out so that the packer cannot change it.
Sample Flow
Scenario 2: Multi-Item Order with only "Item with Box" products
After scanning the first product:
Shipment Package Type
will automatically be set to
"Item's Own Box"
.
Length, Width, Height, and Weight
fields will be populated based on the product's configured dimensions and weight.
Shipment Package Type
dropdown will be grayed out so that the packer cannot change it.
Once the next product is scanned,
Close Pack
button will be auto-triggered , even if
"Prevent Multiple Packages"
is enabled.
Sample Flow:
Scenario 3: Multi-Item Order with both "Item with Box" and normal products
If the packer starts packing the order by scanning a regular product:
The user can continue scanning other regular products into the same shipment package.
The weight will be calculated based on the scanned product’s weight and the LP type’s empty weight.
Shipment Package Type
and dimensions will be filled based on the LP type.
However, if the packer scans an "Item with Box" product:
Shipment Package Type
will automatically be set to
"Item's Own Box"
.
Length, Width, Height, and Weight
fields will be populated based on the product's configured dimensions and weight.
Shipment Package Type
dropdown will be grayed out so that the packer cannot change it.
Once the next product is scanned,
Close Pack
button will be auto-triggered , even if
"Prevent Multiple Packages"
is enabled.

title: Dynamic Replenishment
content:
Overview
Dynamic replenishment is designed to optimize inventory management at picking locations. This feature ensures that product levels are maintained between a defined minimum and maximum capacity by considering the product’s demand.
Goal
The primary goal of dynamic replenishment is to ensure efficient inventory management by maintaining adequate stock levels at desired locations. By dynamically adjusting inventory levels based on demand, this feature helps prevent stockouts and overstock situations.
How It Works & How to Setup Dynamic Replenishment
Dynamic replenishment operates by continuously monitoring product levels at target locations and replenishing inventory as needed. The overview of the entire cycle can be seen below, as to explain how dynamic replenishment works.
1- Setting Replenishment Levels on Products:
Replenishment rules must be defined for products. Two strategies are available for defining these levels:
Global
or
Per Warehouse
.
Replenishment Strategy:
Global:
This is the standard configuration. A single
Min. Replenishment Level
and
Max. Replenishment Level
are defined. These values are applied to
every
warehouse where the product is stored.
Per Warehouse:
This strategy provides granular control. When selected, the global fields are hidden, and a "Per Warehouse" grid is displayed to manage specific warehouse levels.
Configuration of Per Warehouse Levels:
Per Warehouse
is selected as the Replenishment Strategy.
The
Add Replenishment Level
function is used to open the selection modal.
Specific Warehouse(s) are selected from the list.
The
Min
and
Max
levels are entered for these warehouses.
The configuration is saved.
Important Note on "Per Warehouse" Logic:
If the "Per Warehouse" strategy is selected, replenishment tasks are generated
only
for the warehouses explicitly defined in the grid. If a warehouse is missing from the list, the product is
skipped
for that location, and no replenishment task is created.
To learn more about how to create products, please visit this
article.
Also check how to create Warehouse-Based Replenishment Levels in bulk, by using the excel import in this
article
.
2- Configuring Location Settings
Source locations should have the
source
option selected in the
replenishment location type
field.
Target locations must have the
replenishment location type
set to
target.
3- Creating Replenishment Job Types
Establish a dedicated replenishment job type to manage dynamic replenishment tasks.
Replenishment Type
field should be selected as
Dynamic
Allow Suggest Another parameter allows you to retrieve an alternative target location during the put phase of the replenishment.
4- Assigning a dedicated Putaway Algorithm for Dynamic Replenishment:
Create or assign a putaway algorithm to handle replenishment jobs, determining target locations for restocking.
The selected algorithm can be assigned for the dynamic replenishment by marking the "
Use this algorithm as dynamic replenishment algorithm"
checkbox.
A template is available for your dynamic replenenishment algorithm(REPLENISHMENT_ALGORITHM), however, the algorithm can be customized by adding conditions, actions, order by settings or adding if else rules.
Each account can utilize one unique algorithm for replenishment, if another algorithm is assigned for the dynamic replenishment, prior algorithm will become passive.
At least 1 Replenishment Algorithm will remain in the system.
To learn more about how to utilize putaway algorithms, please check this
article
.
5- Running Job Waves & Calculating Replenishment Quantity:
When job waves are executed, the system evaluates inventory levels and creates replenishment jobs if the defined conditions are met.
Replenishment Logic:
If the strategy is
Global
, the product's main Min/Max fields are utilized.
If the strategy is
Per Warehouse
, the specific Min/Max values defined for that warehouse are retrieved.
Replenishment jobs are created if the following condition is met:
(Replenishment Min Level + Open Order Product Qty) > Total Product Inventory at Target Locations
If this condition is satisfied, the replenishment quantity is calculated as:
ReplenishmentQty =Replenishment Max Level + Open Order Product Qty - Total Product Inventory at Target Locations - Job Quantity
If the Max value is 0, the Min value is used in calculation.
To learn more about how to create wave rules for replenishment, please check this
article
.
6- Executing Replenishment Tasks:
Replenishment tasks are carried out via the mobile app. The putaway algorithm we select for dynamic replenishment identifies the target location for the put phase.
Depending on the selection within the replenishment job type, users can utilize the "Suggest Another Location" feature for alternative put locations.
7- Dynamic Replenishment Report
Users can get an overview of the replenishment process using the dynamic replenishment report.
This report displays each product's minimum and maximum replenishment levels, total quantity and total free quantity at source locations, available quantity at target locations, open order quantity, open replenishment task quantity (existing replenishment task quantity), and the quantity needed for further replenishment.
For further information, please check
Dynamic Replenishment Report Article.
Benefits of Dynamic Replenishment
Optimized Inventory Levels:
Maintains product levels at desired locations efficiently.
Increased Efficiency:
Reduces the need for manual intervention and frequent stock checks.
Enhanced Accuracy:
Uses predefined algorithms to ensure accurate replenishment.
Conclusion
Dynamic replenishment is an essential feature to maintain optimal inventory levels at picking locations, ensuring efficient warehouse operations and meeting demand without overstocking. By following the setup steps, you can leverage this feature to streamline your inventory management processes.
​

title: Create an Allocation Algorithm
content:
Logiwa's allocation algorithms will help create a more efficient picking process for your operations. With the right parameters, you can create an algorithm that will streamline your picking jobs and make sure everything runs without a hitch. This article will walk you through that process.
Guide to Creating an Allocation Algorithm
First, navigate to
Algorithms
screen.
If you have trouble finding the screen, please use the
Search Option
on the menu bar.
Select
Allocation Algorithm
from the available options.
You will see the allocation algorithm table, which includes a default algorithm for new accounts.
Expand to learn more about the default allocation algorithm.
The default allocation algorithm includes those rules:
Don't allocate damaged inventory
Order by ascending
Area Type
(Picking, Storage, Receiving, Returns, Packing, Shipment, Kitting)
Order by ascending
Picking Priority
Order by ascending
Lot Batch Number
Order by ascending
Expiry Date
To continue with algorithm creation, select
Create Allocation Algorithm
from the right side of the screen.
Primary Information
A menu with the header
Create Allocation Algorithm
will display. The
Primary Information
tab will load first.
Enter values for the following fields:
Algorithm Name*:
Type the algorithm's name in the system. We recommend a simple and recognizable name.
Warehouse*:
Select the relevant warehouse from a dropdown menu.
Active:
Set the algorithm as active (
Yes
) or inactive (
No
). It must be set to active to be used.
Click on
Save and Proceed
.
Rules
Next, you need to define some rules for the algorithm. Press the
Create New
button to create a rule.
Begin by entering a name in the
Rule Name
field.
Order Conditions
Second, you'll need to set a condition by selecting the
Plus (+)
button next to
Order Conditions
.
Some key details about conditions:
A condition is what triggers the activation of your rule.
The condition can be set to apply to all situations or a specific condition.
You can define single or multiple conditions for one rule.
If you select
Apply to All
, this will apply the created rule to all allocation actions. Click
Add
to continue.
If you select
Specify Condition
, you can set a variety of conditional statements, starting with the
If
that you select. The available options will vary depending on your initial
If
selection.
For example, two conditions from MyClient's Wholesale orders:
Select the
Add
button to save your condition.
Below you can see the conditions on the rule board. When you add more than one condition, those conditions will be connected with
AND.
By doing this, you can create an algorithm for situations that satisfy both conditions.
You can add additional conditions to this rule by clicking the
Plus (+)
that appears next to the first condition, or use the
Edit
or
Delete
buttons to make changes.
Target Conditions
Next, you can define target conditions for your rule. From that section, you can determine to which location inventory will be allocated.
For example, you can put a rule for your damage inventory by selecting a damage reason.
Order By
In the final section, you can also add
Order By
for your algorithm. Order by section allows you to specify the order in which inventory will be allocated.
For example, you can define a rule for your product's expiry date and select the sorting method as ascending. With this setting, you can first allocate your products with the closest expiration dates.
Finally, save your rule by clicking the
Save Rule
button.
You will receive a confirmation message if the rule was saved successfully.
Additionally, you can add more than one rule for the algorithm. To change the priority for these rules, drag and drop them using the 3-lines icon on the right side of the rule list.

title: Logiwa IO New Features Early Access (Beta) Program
content:
Overview
Our Features Early Access Program gives select customers early access to new features on our platform. By participating, you can explore our latest functionalities, share valuable feedback, and help shape Logiwa’s product capabilities. This approach enables us to fine-tune features based on real-world usage, ensuring they align with customer needs before launching the GA version.
How It Works
Early Access Invitation:
Selected customers are invited to try out features with a “Beta” tag in the Logiwa platform. This tag indicates that the feature has been fully developed and tested and is now available in Beta for real-world feedback.
Testing & Feedback:
Early Access customers interact with new features, provide direct feedback, and help us identify any potential improvements.
Feature Enhancement & Release:
After collecting the feedback from the customers and validation, features that meet our confidence metrics will be fully released to all customers. The “Beta” tag will be removed, and the feature will be announced in our release notes.
Important Considerations
Impact of Testing:
As “Beta” features are released recently, certain functionalities might change based on feedback, and there may be minor performance adjustments before the full launch.
How to Provide Feedback
Participants can share their experiences through feedback channels designated for each feature. These feedback options may include an embedded survey, form, Customer Success Manager, or customer support contact point.
Legal Disclaimer
Participation in Logiwa’s Features Early Access Program is entirely voluntary. By accessing a feature with a “Beta” tag, customers acknowledge that the feature is in the Beta version and may undergo minor refinements. Logiwa does not assume liability for any financial claims, including but not limited to business interruptions or revenue loss, that may arise due to the feature’s functionality or temporary issues.

title: Configuring  Third-Party Billing and Taxes & Duties Payor
content:
Overview
Logiwa IO enables you to bill shipping charges for both domestic and international orders to various parties, including the sender, receiver, or a third-party entity such as your clients or a different third-party entity. Properly configuring these settings ensures accurate shipping charge allocation, streamlines international customs billing processes, and enhances billing flexibility for your clients.
Configuration: Setting Up a Third-Party Billing Account for a Carrier
To bill shipping charges to a third party, you must first add their account information to the relevant carrier's configuration.
Navigate to Carrier Management:
Go to integrations > Shipping.
Select the Carrier:
Locate and select the carrier for which you want to add a third-party billing account.
Access Third Party Account Settings:
Within the carrier's configuration advanced screen, find the
Third Party Account
section.
Add a New Account:
Click the
Add Account
button. This will open the "Add Third Party Account" pop-up window.
Enter Account Details:
Fill in the required fields:
Account Number:
The third party's account number.
Country:
The country associated with the third party's billing address (must be a two-letter country code, e.g., US, CA, GB)
Postal Code:
The postal code for the third party's billing address.
6.
Save the Account:
Click
Save
to add the third-party account to the carrier's profile.
Applying Billing and Tax Information to Shipment Orders
Once the setup is complete, you can apply the billing settings to individual or multiple shipment orders. This can be done manually, through an Excel import, via an API, or automated with a workflow.
Option 1: Manual Setup
When creating or editing a shipment order, you can specify the billing and tax details in the following fields under the shipment tab:
Carrier Billing Type:
Determines who pays for the shipping charges. Common options include:
Sender:
Your account is billed.
Recipient:
The recipient of the package is billed.
Third Party:
A pre-configured third-party account is billed.
Collect
Prepaid
Charged Account Number:
For shipping charges, If "Third Party" is selected, select the corresponding predefined third party account number here.
Carrier Int’l Billing Type:
Determines who pays for the duties and taxes on international shipments. Options are typically similar to the domestic billing type (e.g., Prepaid, Recipient, Third Party).
Int’l Charged Account Number:
If a third party is paying for international duties and taxes, select their predefined account number here.
Option 2: Excel Setup
To efficiently configure numerous shipment orders at once, you can perform a bulk import using the Excel spreadsheet formatted with the specific column headers for billing and tax information.
Option 3: API
For more details, please refer to the following
guide
Option 4: Workflow

title: Product Listings
content:
Many of our users sell their products through a number of channels, and we realize that some of your products may have different details depending on the channel they are sold through. That's why the
Product Listings
section of Logiwa exists. From this page, you can see all the listings of a given product in one place.
Article Contents
View Product Listings

Your Product Listings
View Product Listings
To view your product listings, click on the
Product Listings
button under
Settings.
If you haven't linked any sales channels, this section will be blank. If you have, you will see listings of your products across your channels.
Product Listings Creation
We match products based on their SKU across your sales channels. If products on these channels have the same SKU number, we automatically link them together and create listings.
If you have the same SKU numbers within one sales channel, the process is the same. We create only one product with reference to the SKU, and create listings for others.
Listings and Inventory
Unlike the products in your Logiwa inventory, listings do not represent the number of products you have in inventory. Thus, you may see many listings across all of your sales channels for one product, but the product itself only has one stock quantity.
Your Product Listings
You only have to do one thing to add product listings into Logiwa. When you integrate with your sales channels, we'll create the listings automatically!

Overview
Logiwa IO’s Excel import feature allows you to efficiently create one or more count plans in bulk. This method is ideal for managing large or recurring counts without having to create each plan manually. This guide will walk you through the process of preparing your file and importing it into the system.
Step-by-Step Guide
Step 1: Prepare Your Excel File
Before importing, you must prepare an Excel file (
.xlsx
or
.csv
) with the correct information. You can download a pre-formatted template directly from the import screen in Logiwa.
There are two separate templates for creating count plans: one for
Location Counts
and one for
SKU Counts
.
Location Count Template Columns:
Location Code (Mandatory)
: The exact code of the location to be counted.
Count Plan Code (Mandatory)
: The unique code for the count plan. To include multiple locations in the same plan, use the same Count Plan Code for each location row.
Description
: An optional description for the count plan.
Scheduled Count Date:
The date the count is scheduled for, in yyyy-MM-dd format.
Lock Locations:
Enter YES or NO.
SKU Count Template Columns:
SKU Code (Mandatory):
The exact SKU of the product to be counted.
Count Plan Code (Mandatory):
The unique code for the count plan.
Description
: An optional description for the count plan.
Scheduled Count Date:
The date the count is scheduled for, in yyyy-MM-dd format.
Lock Locations:
Enter YES or NO.
Step 2: Access the Import Feature
Navigate to
Inventory
>
Count Plan
.
Click the
Import
button in the top-right corner and select
Import Count Plan
.
Step 3: Upload and Validate Your File
On the import screen, drag and drop your prepared Excel file or click to browse and select the file from your computer.
Click
Upload
.
The system will display a preview, matching the columns from your file to the fields in Logiwa. A green checkmark indicates a successful match. If you see a red X, manually select the correct Logiwa field from the dropdown menu to resolve the mismatch.
Once all columns are matched, click the
Import
button to finalize the process.
Step 4: Review Import Results
After the import is complete, you can review the results on the import history screen. If the
Error Count
is greater than 0, click
Details
to see which rows failed and the specific reason for each failure.
Troubleshooting Common Import Errors
If your import fails, check for these common issues:
Duplicate Entry Error:
The system will fail the import if the same
Location Code
or
SKU Code
is listed more than once under the same
Count Plan Code
. Each location or SKU must be unique within a single plan.
Inconsistent Plan Data Error:
For a single
Count Plan Code
, all rows must have the exact same
Description
,
Scheduled Count Date
, and
Lock Locations
value. If these fields have conflicting information across different rows of the same plan, the import will fail.
Invalid Code Error:
The
Location Code
or
SKU Code
in your file does not exist in the selected warehouse. Ensure all codes are valid before importing.
Unique Count Plan Code:
The
Count Plan Code
must have a unique value.
What's Next?
Once your count plan has been successfully imported, the next step is to create a job to be executed by your warehouse team. To proceed, you must have a
Count Job Type
configured in the system.
To learn how to configure a job type, read our guide:
Create a Job Type for a Cycle Count
.
After your job type is ready, you can create jobs manually from the Count Plan screen or automate their creation for recurring counts by setting up a
Cycle Count Wave Rule
.
To learn how to automate job creation, read our guide:
Create Wave Rules for a Cycle Count
.
Couldn’t Find What You Were Looking For?
Visit our
Help Center
to search more documents!

Import Purchase Order via Excel File
Import Inventory via Excel File
Import Locations via Excel File

title: Total Inventory Report
content:
The Total Inventory Report provides a comprehensive, high-level overview of your product inventory quantities across your entire network or specific warehouses. Unlike reports focusing on specific locations or availability for future orders (like ATP), this report gives a consolidated snapshot of total physical stock, including breakdowns of undamaged and damaged quantities, alongside current sales order commitments.
It's an essential tool for strategic inventory analysis, understanding overall stock value, and identifying system-wide inventory levels for specific products.
Location
To access the report, navigate to the
Inventory
section or use the main search bar. Enter "Total Inventory" and select the report from the results.
Utilizing the Total Inventory Report
This report is valuable for gaining a broad perspective on your inventory:
Consolidated View:
By default, it aggregates inventory data across all warehouses defined in your system, offering a complete picture of a product's stock footprint. You can also filter by specific warehouses to drill down.
Stock Status Analysis:
Clearly differentiates between
Total Quantity
(including damaged items) and
Undamaged Quantity
, allowing for quick assessment of sellable vs. non-sellable stock levels network-wide. The
Damaged Qty
column pinpoints the exact amount of non-sellable stock.
Availability Insights:
Incorporates
Open SO Qty
to show how much total stock and
undamaged stock
is currently committed. The
Available UOM Quantity
and
Undamaged Available UOM Qty
columns calculate the remaining quantities after these commitments are considered.
Product Details:
Includes key product identifiers and categorizations like SKU, Product Name, Product Type, Product Group, and Kit Type for easy reference and filtering. Displays the primary Image associated with the product.
Efficient Navigation:
Hyperlinks within the report grid facilitate quick access to related information:
Clicking a
SKU
navigates to the
Product List
screen, filtered for the specific client and SKU.
Clicking the
Open SO Qty
directs you to the
Shipment Order Backlo
g screen, filtered by client and SKU (and warehouse if specified).
Clicking the
Damaged Qty
takes you to the I
nventory by Location
screen, filtered to show only the damaged inventory locations for that client and SKU (across all warehouses unless filtered).
Clicking the
Kit Type
navigates to the
Kit Inventory Report
, filtered by client and SKU (and warehouse if specified).
How the Total Inventory Report Works
Consolidation:
The report aggregates inventory quantities for each product across all warehouses unless a specific warehouse is selected in the filters.
Product-Centric:
Each row represents a unique product (SKU) managed within the system for a specific client.
UOM Based:
All quantity fields reflect the product's standard Unit of Measure (UOM).
Real-Time:
Reflects current inventory levels and open order commitments based on the latest system data. Significant inventory changes (receipts, shipments, adjustments) will update the report's figures.
Column Explanations
The table below details the columns typically found in the Total Inventory report, their descriptions, calculation logic where applicable, and corresponding Open API fields.
The Open API method to obtain this report as followed:
GET /v{version}/Report/TotalInventory/i/{index}/s/{size}
Note
: Please use version as 3.1 to retrieve the most updated version of the endpoint.
Field
Description
Formula
Open API Field
Image
Displays the default image associated with the product.
N/A
productDefaultImageLink
Warehouse
Indicates the warehouse(s) the data pertains to. Shows "All Warehouses" by default, or a specific warehouse code if filtered.
N/A
warehouseCode
Client
The client account associated with the inventory record.
N/A
clientDisplayName
SKU
The Stock Keeping Unit (unique identifier) for the product.
N/A
productSku
Product Name
The descriptive name of the product.
N/A
productName
Product Type
The classification or category assigned to the product
N/A
productTypeName
Product Group
A broader grouping assigned to the product
N/A
productGroupName
Kit Type
Identifies if the product is 'Kit to Stock', 'Kit to Order', or not a kit.
N/A
kitTypeName (kitTypeId)
Total Quantity
The total physical quantity (UOM) of the item across the specified warehouse scope (all or filtered), including any damaged inventory.
(Undamaged Qty) + (Damaged Qty)
totalQuantity
Undamaged Quantity
The total physical quantity (UOM) of the item within the specified scope, excluding any damaged inventory.
(Total Qty) - (Damaged Qty)
undamagedQuantity
Damaged Qty

Sum of damaged inventory records.

The total physical quantity (UOM), including damaged items, remaining after subtracting commitments to open shipment orders.
(Total Quantity) - (Open SO Qty)

The quantity (UOM) of undamaged inventory remaining after subtracting commitments to open sales orders.
(Undamaged Quantity) - (Open SO Qty)

title: Who can manage clients?
content:
Logiwa IO includes 4 different user types, and each user type plays different roles for the account. In this article, we explain the user type's access levels and their effects to manage clients.
User Types
Logiwa IO has 4 different user types:  Owner, Operation User, Admin Client User,  and Client User.
Owner
The Owner user, the user who created the Logiwa account.
In Logiwa there can be only one Owner user for an account.
An Owner user has access to every function of the purchased sales package. The owner user can see, edit, delete, create, change, or add any data within the system. The owner will have access automatically to any client created in the system.
As a summary, the owner user is will be available to create, edit, see, delete, or change any client data or client-related data within the system.
Operation User
The operation user mostly refers to users who work for the fulfillment company. They can be pickers, packers, receivers, or a warehouse supervisor, etc.
An Operation user has access to only warehouse operations-related functions. They cannot access any account, company, or client settings-related data.
In summary, the operation user does not have access to manage clients. He can not create, change, edit, or delete any client-specific settings.
Admin Client User
The Admin Client User mostly refers to the admin user of a client. The user still is a client user, but it has more access than an ordinary client user.
The Admin Client User's access level is defined to manage client specific definitions, preferences, and users. For example, an admin client user can set up client preferences such as Currency or Language.  But the user cannot access any account or company-related data. An admin client user has access to the functionality of a Client User as well. An admin client user is a more powerful user than a client user but a less powerful user in comparison to the owner user.
We're highly suggesting having only one Admin Client User for a client.
Client User
The Client User is a standard client user.
The Client User's access level is limited to see reports and the client's own data such as orders or products. They have access to edit, delete, and create orders.
Need to note that, access levels of each client user role can be varied. Admin Client User can limit client user rights. For example, delete access may not be given to any client user.

title: 02/07/2024 Release Notes
content:
What’s New/Improved
LogiwaIO now supports the
Spanish language
!
To enable Spanish in LogiwaIO, go to the "My Profile" section and adjust the language settings.
The
Kit Product Excel Import
feature is now available from the Product
screen.
In order to create kit products in bulk, initially, the products should be created by using our Product Create Excel Import function. Then, the Kit Product Excel Import feature can be used to mark your products as “Kit products” by defining their components.
Product Pack Type Import
functionality has been added to the Product screen.
A new
permission for the “Change Attributes” button
on the Inventory by Location screen has been added to the Roles screen.
Tags
functionality is now available on the
Purchase Order screen
. You can now attach multiple customizable tags with colors to your purchase orders. These tags are also editable in bulk, meaning that if you make changes to the original tag, all assigned tags will be updated upon confirmation. These tags can be used in your custom algorithms or workflows as specific conditions.
Two new actions
are now available for the
Putaway Algorithm
:
Suggest a location that has inventory of the same SKU & same pack type.
Suggest a location that has inventory of this selected pack type.
Putting away products with the Parent LP
option is now possible on the mobile Transfer screen.
Batch Label Printing at the Packing Station
is now available in LogiwaIO!
This feature can be enabled in the Packing Station by setting up the "Disable Batch Order Packing" parameter as FALSE from the Client setup.
With this development, when scanning a tote/location in the Packing screen, the system checks identical orders (in terms of SKU and quantity) and allows bulk order packing and label generation.
Recommended for use in Identical Item Batch Pick jobs and Identical Order Batch Pick jobs with AI!
Two
new shipment order statuses
are now available:
Ready to Load:
When picking and the packing tasks are completed and only loading tasks remain, the order status changes to Ready to Load.
Loading Started:
If at least one loading task is completed for the order and there are still pending loading tasks, the order status changes to Loading Started.
Change Log
feature has been integrated into the following screens:
Shipment Plan and Role Permissions
.
All related changes can be monitored from the Change Log.
We have also enhanced the
Changed To
and
Changed From
columns, making them clearer for users to understand the changes that have been made.
Order Codes Hyperlink
has been added under the Shipment Plan Orders and Shipment Plan LPs tabs.
Buttons on the Shipment Order
screen have been updated for better functionality and design.
“Job Priority”
field has been added to the job list grid under the Job Management screen.
“Wave Priority”
field has been added to the wave list grid under the Wave Rules screen.
LP Number Excel Import
is now available in LogiwaIO! LP Numbers can be created in bulk by using this function.
Warehouse Prefix
has been added to
LP Type filters/dropdowns
for better warehouse identification.
Error codes
have been added to the message field
during the label creation process
.
Now, users will be able to see carrier error codes along with error messages.
Shopify
setups are now configured to
manage different tokens
for each process.
This feature will support high transaction volume with Shopify to avoid throttle limits.
Shopify
setup can be configured to
manage multiple locations
. Thus, it enables users to pull orders from different locations into different warehouses within LogiwaIO.
Sales price
on shipment order grid will be shown based on
store currencies
for WooCommerce and Shopify.
Product image
type
now includes the
.webp format
.
Custom Carrier Integration
now supports
ZPL and EPL label formats
.
Shopify variant items
now have a more detailed description in LogiwaIO as “Item + Variant Description.”
The UPS
connection now supports
different currencies
.
UPS, FedEx, and EasyPost
carrier connections can now have
rates
and
labels with different dimension metrics
.
There are a few
improvements in the 3PL Billing
module (listed below):
We have added "Unit Price," "From Quantity," and "To Quantity" fields to the Consolidated Billing Report.
In our "Shipment" operation type, we have introduced the "Fee by: Per LP" option.
This new feature allows you to seamlessly capture your LP shipments using our billing module.
We've added a bulk delete option for previously created billing contracts.
VAS Notes entered in the VAS Operations screen are now available in the Detailed Billing Report.
There are a few
improvements in the Return
module (listed below):
At the Return Station you can now enter returned product’s serial numbers (primary & secondary), and the “Serial Number Match” parameter can be enabled in the Data Setup screen to ensure only shipped serial numbers can be returned.
At the return station, you can now track expiration dates and lot numbers. “Lot Batch Number Match” and “Expiry Date Match” parameters can be enabled in the Data Setup screen to ensure only shipped attributes can be returned.
Additionally, our system adapts to different date formats to make the return process as efficient as possible.
Excel Export function
has been added to the screens below:
Fulfillment
Shipment Plan
End of the Day Report
Job Management
Automation
Workflows
Rate Shopping
Reports and Analytics
Change Log
Serial Number Transaction History
Integration History
Integration Status
Orders and Shipments
Products and Inventory
Settings
Product Listing
Vendor List
Warehouse
Mobile Carts
Shipment Packages
Job Types
Billing Report
VAS Operations
Users
Roles
What's Fixed
The issue of clients being displayed on the Main Dashboard, even when the user does not have access to these clients, has been resolved.
Client’s Billing Address saving issue has been fixed.
If there is an error during import, The import status used to remain at “Started”. This issue has been fixed.
A button malfunction while adding the 10th custom field has been fixed.
Saving issue for kit product barcodes has been fixed.
If orders with kit to order products were downloaded from sales channels, the kit to order product was not being divided into its components. This issue has been fixed.
The issue where changes to the components of kit products were not reflected on the screen has been resolved.
A minor issue in editing shipment packages has been fixed.
Captured image quality of the damaged products has been significantly increased.
From the Count screen (Mobile), locations will be displayed according to walking path priority.
Previously, when there was free stock in the mobile cart even though the mobile cart status was Occupied, an error message was being displayed during the picking execution step. Now, this error displays earlier, when the mobile cart is first scanned.
The issue with editing existing billing lines has been fixed.
Change Log was showing the date 3 hours to early for transactions made on mobile screens. Now, this issue has been fixed and Change Log displays the correct date.
Change Log no longer shows extra logs as empty for unchanged fields in Shipment Order and Purchase Order updates.
A minor dislocation issue with text in workflow structure has been corrected.
The issue with cloning actions when using Add SKU or Delete SKU actions more than once in each workflow block has been resolved.
The issue of screen resetting, which occurred when dropdowns were modified in different workflow actions, has been resolved. Now, subsequent dropdowns will accurately display relevant items when the selection in the previous dropdown is changed.
During packing list creation on the Printouts screen, there was a minor saving issue about store-based packing lists. This issue has been solved.
Some grid columns data structure in the Serial Receiving and Serial Shipment History reports have been improved.
API/Webhooks
Introducing our enhanced ShipmentPlan Open API, featuring a newly designed endpoint to streamline the creation of shipment plans along with orders, enabling effortless listing, updating, and deletion of shipment plans. Experience the ease of handling shipment plans with our improved API, designed for efficiency and flexibility!
Client and Warehouse related shipment package validations have been added to the Shipment Order Create and Edit methods in Open API.
Customer Create, Update, and List endpoints are now available in Open API.
FromInventoryIdentifier and ToInventoryIdentifier fields have been added to the TransactionHistoryReport Open API endpoint.

title: Cancel a Purchase Order
content:
You may need to cancel a purchase order due to invalid information, a mistake during creation, or a number of other reasons. With just a few clicks, you can cancel a purchase order, as long as it is still in the
Pending
status.
Step-by-Step Guide
First, navigate to the
Purchase Orders
screen.
If you cannot find the screen, please use the
Search Option
on the menu bar.
Choose a purchase order or orders with the
Pending
status.
Select
Cancel Order
.
A pop-up asking if you want to cancel the selected order or orders will be displayed.
Keep in mind that after cancelling an order, you cannot update it anymore.
Click
Yes
to proceed.
You will receive a confirmation message if the order was successfully cancelled.
You can also check if the order was cancelled from the table.
Alternatively, you can view/edit a specific purchase order with the
Pending
status and directly click the
Cancel Order
button in the upper right corner.
A pop-up asking if you want to cancel the order will be displayed. Click on
Yes
to proceed.
You can now see if the order status has changed to
Cancelled
from
Pending
.

title: Design a Retailer Label for Case
content:
The Retailer Case Label Printout is a printout designed to generate case-specific labels required for retailer compliance processes. These labels can be customized to include essential information such as UCC (SSCC18) numbers, product details, and other retailer-required identifiers. Each label is applied to a case before the picking process begins to ensure that cases can be correctly validated and scanned during fulfillment.
To begin, navigate to the “Printouts & Labels” screen.
Find and click on the “Retailer Label for Case” icon.
Click on the “
Create Printout
” button.
The “Create New Printout” sidebar will open. You'll first fill in the fields in the
Step 1
section. The fields here are explained below.
Field Name
Description
Name*
Name for printout.
Description*
Longer name or description for printout.
Report Type*
Automatically selected
Records per Page*
Select from single records or multiple records per page.
Print Mode*
Select whether you wish to print immediately, view a PDF preview, or view a report preview.
Print Type*
Select laser or label printer.
Status
Toggle to set this label as active or inactive.
Click
Next
to move to
Step 2
In
Step 2
, you'll be presented with
ready-to-use templates
for the most common retailer label formats, such as Walmart, TJMaxx, Target, Nordstrom, etc. These templates can save time by providing preformatted label designs based on retailer requirements.
Click
Next
to move to
Step 3
.
The Logiwa printout designer will open automatically in another tab. If it doesn't, click on the “Go to the Logiwa Report Designer” link.
The report designer is a WYSIWYG tool that allows you to drag and drop, resize, reformat, and remove content.
You can learn more about using it here.
Once you're finished, click on the
Report
button to access the
Save
button. You'll receive a confirmation message when the save is successful.
Return to the
Create New Printout
sidebar and click
Next
to move to
Step 4
.
In
Step 4
, you'll select which
clients
will have access to this new label design by switching the
Access
toggle. At least one client must be selected.
Click
Next
to move to
Step 5.
In
Step 5
, you'll assign this label design to a
Retailer
. You can only select one retailer per each design.
Once all selections are made, click
Next
to finalize your label. A confirmation message will appear if it is saved successfully.
If you need to make further modifications to your printout, click the
3-Dots menu
to find the Show Details, Edit, Duplicate, Change Log, and Delete buttons.

title: Shipium Integration
content:
Shipium coordinates your carriers, contracts, rules, and shipping operations to help reduce delivery costs 12%. Customers turn to Shipium to help make a promise they can keep, then keep the promise that they made.  If you use Shipium, it can be connected to Logiwa in just a few steps.
Initial Setup
Navigate to the
Integrations > Shipping
page to create the carrier/shipping integration.
If you have trouble finding this page, please use the
Search
option.
Select
Shipium
from the available options:
You can now fill in the necessary fields to create the Shipium connection. You will need the following information from Shipium:
API Key*:
The
ApiKey
field in your Shipium account.
Once you've entered the API information, choose whether this account will be a test account or not. If it is a test account, select
Yes
. If it is not a test account, select
No
.
Click
Continue
to proceed with setup.
You will now enter additional information about the setup, beginning with the
General
tab.
General
In this tab, enter the following information:
Setup Name*:
The name that will be used in the system for this carrier connection.
Warehouse*:
Select the warehouse that will use this carrier connection.
Active:
Select
Yes
for an active carrier connection or
No
for inactive.
After entering this information, click the
Next
button to proceed.
Clients
In the
Clients
tab, you will choose which clients can or cannot access this carrier connection.
To assign access to this carrier connection to all clients, select the
All Clients
button.
To assign access to some clients and not others, choose
Select Manually
.
You can now enable/disable access to this carrier connection by selecting the clients you wish to change access for and clicking the coinciding
Disable
or
Enable
buttons.
Once you have selected the clients who will use this connection, click the
Next
button.
Services
In the
Services
tab, you will choose which carrier services can or cannot be accessed with this carrier connection. The services offered here will vary depending on the services you have available from this carrier.
To assign access to all current and future services from this carrier, select the
Use All Services
button ot authoriz
To assign which services will be used manually, click
Select Manually
.
You can now enable/disable access to specific services by selecting the service(s) you wish to change access for and clicking the coinciding
Disable
or
Enable
buttons.
Once you have selected services to be used with this connection, click the
Next
button.
Packages
In the
Packages
tab, you will choose which shipment packages (boxes, etc.) that can or cannot be used with this carrier connection.
To assign access to all current and future packages from this carrier, select the
All Packages
button.
To assign which shipment packages will be used manually, click
Select Manually
.
You can now enable/disable access to specific packages by selecting the package(s) you wish to change access for and clicking the coinciding
Disable
or
Enable
buttons.
Once you have selected packages to be used with this connection, click the
Next
button.
Advanced
In this section, you will find all advanced options available for the carrier, including mark-ups, ship from and return addresses, third-party accounts, and additional messages for labels. These are not required, but they will help further customize your carrier connection to meet your business needs.
Click the sections below to learn more about each advanced option.
Markup Rate
Select the
Plus (+)
icon next to Markup Rate to open the Markup Rate pop-up.
For
Markup Type
, select
Percentage
or
Fixed Price
.
If
Percentage
is selected, you will enter
Markup Amount
by percent.
If
Fixed Price
is selected, you will enter a specific price for the
Markup Amount
. The currency used will be the default currency for your account.
Click
Save
to record the markup you've entered.
You can now
Edit
or
Delete
this markup by using the corresponding icons.
Ship From Location
For this section, either fill in a different
Ship From
address to use when using this carrier, or select
Use Warehouse Address
and choose the relevant warehouse to automatically fill in the address.
Third-Party Account
Third-party billing accounts are unavailable via Shipium at this time so this section should be skipped.
Label Settings
Label messages enable users to add extra chosen fields to the carrier label. All chosen label messages will be printed on the label, in addition to the default information of the label. The number of label messages needed may differ from carrier to carrier. The available fields are listed in each label message drop-down.
For example, if you would like to add the store name to all printed labels from this carrier, select
StoreName
from the dropdown.
Finalization
After choosing or skipping the
Advanced
options, click
Finish
to complete your new carrier setup.
You will be returned to the shipping integrations page. You will receive a confirmation message and also be able to see your new Shipium connection.

Create labels
Void labels
End-of-Day Report

Third-party accounts

title: 05/08/2024 Release Notes
content:
As the month of May unfolds, we're here to bring you a fresh batch of updates tailored to upgrade your operations, Notable highlights include enhancements to the Billing module's options, work orders for kit-to-stock products, expanded search functionalities for locations, improvements to packing instructions, and much more. Let's dive in.
Work Orders and Kit to Stock
Work orders can be used to track the kitting process of kit-to-stock products.
Each work order can be generated for a single unique kit-to-stock product. The work order lines consist of components for the kit-to-stock product, which are
specified during the kit-to-stock product setup
, while quantities are obtained from the
Product setup
. Roles can be granted access to work orders through settings, and various access settings can be defined and enabled or disabled for existing user roles.
Work order creation can be either
done from the Work Order screen or on the Kit Inventory Report scre
en by selecting the kit-to-stock product on the report. Work orders can be
created for stock, which allows the search for a kit-to-stock product of the selected client directly.
Alternatively,
work orders can be created for shipment orders, which allows the search for a shipment order of the selected client that contains kit-to-stock products.
The kit-to-stock products of the selected order can be included in the work order. Please note that the
Built for SO
option is
solely aimed at enhancing the selection of kit-to-stock products at present.
This option is not currently integrated with Shipment Order Allocation.
Click below to learn more about the new work order types, job types, use in allocation and picking, and the create kit process.
More Information on Work Orders
Work Order Type Management
Work order types can be managed under
Data Setup.
Based on the
Backflush
parameter in the
Work Order Type
setup, work orders have two different life cycles:
If
Backflush is disabled:
Work orders need to be allocated and picking tasks will be created afterward.
In order to proceed to kitting, picking tasks must be completed on the mobile app.
If
Backflush is enabled:
The component picking process can be bypassed for bulk kitting operations.
Allocation and picking are not required.
Work Order Job Type Management
A new
Work Orders job operation type is available on the Job Types screen.
Existing allocation algorithms can be used for work order jobs. However,
the settings for Order Conditions in the selected algorithm will be disregarded. Only the configurations for Inventory Conditions and Order By will be taken into account when allocating work orders.
Dedicated work order conditions
can be
selected for specific work order job types
.
Allocation and Picking of Work Orders
The
Warehouse Operations
button on the
Work Order screen allows the allocation of work orders (only non-backflush)
Allocation of work orders is
only possible when using work order job types, and merging into existing job options is only feasible for merging work orders into existing work order jobs.
Wave integration is currently not possible
for work order allocation.
Picking of work orders can be executed using the mobile app
. This process is identical to executing picking tasks for shipment orders.
Creating a picking list is currently not available for work orders
but this development is planned for the future.
Create Kit Process
Once picking for a work order is completed
(not necessary for backflush work orders) the
Create Kit process can be initiated on the Work Order screen.
Source Location/LP entry is
required to validate component inventory.
This search box allows for a search of locations or LPs.
Target Location/LP entry is required to determine where to create kit inventory.
During the kitting process, assembled
kit-to-stock products can be assigned with inventory attributes such as expiry date tracking, production date tracking and lot/batch number tracking
(only if the inventory attributes are enabled for the kit-to-stock product).
Serial number tracking is currently not possible for kit-to-stock products.
Work orders do not support assigning serial numbers during kitting.
Product labels can be created for kit-to-stock product
at the last step of the create kit process.
Completing the create kit process executes inventory transactions
, where component quantities are reduced at the source location/LP and kit-to-stock product quantity is increased at the target location/LP.
Inventory changes can be
tracked on the Transaction History Report.
New records will be created on the
Receiving History Report
for the
created kit-to-stock product inventory.
Disassemble Kit Process
This process can be directly initiated on the
Work Order
screen. Creating work orders is not necessary for the disassemble kit process.
Source Location/LP entry is
required to validate kit-to-stock product inventory.
This search box allows for a search of locations or LPs.
Target Location/LP entry is required to determine where to create component inventory.
During the disassembly process, disassembled
component products can be assigned with inventory attributes such as expiry date tracking, production date tracking and lot/batch number tracking
(only if the inventory attributes are enabled for components.).
Serial number tracking is currently not possible for disassembling kit-to-stock products.
Product labels can be created for component products
at the last step of the disassembly process.
Completing the disassemble kit process executes inventory transactions
, where kit-to-stock product quantity is reduced at the source location/LP and component product quantities are increased at the target location/LP.
Inventory changes can be
tracked on the Transaction History Report.
New records will be created on the
Receiving History Report
for the
created component product inventory.
What's New/Improved
Column size extension
is now available for
reports
.
Users can
now search for locations using either Location Code or Location Barcode when using the Look Up function.
A new section titled
Job Priority & Delete Options has been added to the Wave Rule screen.
This section allows users to
choose priority tags for all jobs in a wave and automate the deletion of pending jobs based on a set frequency.
The
product/line-based packing instructions on the Packing screen
have been updated fo
r improved clarity and usability.
Allow Production Date Swap on Picking
has been added as an option under
Shipment Order Type parameters
. When enabled, this feature
permits users to scan a different production date than those listed in the shipment order
during the picking process.
A Kit Component Inventory Availability Report
has been added to Logiwa.
Report Capabilities:
Search by SKU bar
Filter capabilities
Screen refresh button
Large/small images option
Show [x] items selection
Pagination
Export as Excel function
Total record counter
Grid column customization
Users will now be able to edit and delete pack type details using the
Bulk Import Pack Types and Barcode
functionality.
A new
Product Lookup
screen has been released, allowing users to scan the SKU or barcode of a product and check its the inventory status. Additionally, they can view detailed attributes, such as the lot number and expiration date for a scanned product.
A new
Label Status
column has been added to the
Carrier Shipment Details
report to
display whether the label is cancelled (voided) or not (active).
Billing Updates:
The
Billing module's custom field options have been enhanced
with this update. Previously, some
Operation Types
and
Fee By fields
were
not linked to the custom fields used on the Location, LP, Product, Shipment Plan, Shipment Order, and Purchase Order screens.
Now, the
Operation Type and Fee By fields
associated with custom fields are
now included with their respective comparators
.
A
new condition
named
Total Volume has been added for LPs.
This condition allows users to
define charges per LP, based on the total volume of products located on the LP, including the LP's own volume
defined at the LP Type's screen.
Users can now
exclude a specified number of items from billing calculations
, which can be useful in tier-based pricing scenarios. Users can adjust the exclusion count for specific fees, enabling different pricing for the first item compared to later items.
The introduction of a
new Storage Fee Calculation Type enables users to perform separate counts for storage charges, applicable for Per Location and Per Pallet fee options.
Logiwa IO previously calculated storage charges based on
daily
accumulation, peak or end-of-period inventory.
The new option
enables distinct counting over the entire billing period, counting each LP number or location code only once.
A Pick and Pack Order Based product charge has been added to the system
. This feature allows the billing module to
adjust per-product pick charges based on the number of shipment orders picked,
introducing a new option called
Tier-Order Base
alongside the existing
Tier Base
option.
Existing Tier Base Option:
Checks the total number of products picked during the billing period and selects the appropriate pricing tier.
New Tier-Order Base Option:
Charges per product based on the number of shipment orders picked, adjusting the charge accordingly.
Product Weight and Product Volume conditions
can now
consider the weight and volume information of the selected pack type(s),
rather than just the product's UOM data.
A new
Age Based tab will be added to the Billing screen for storage operations.
This tab allows users to
differentiate between long-term and short-term storage charges and charge for the duration of storage. It is available in Storage Operations for Pallet and Product Fee By options.
New options have been added for
Return
operations:
Operation Type: Returns added as an option.
Fee By: Per SO, Per RMA, Per Product, and Per SKU added.
Charge By Options:
Various
new conditions
depending on the selected Charge By added.
Users can now
edit existing conditions and save those changes
when using the
Edit Billing screen.
The
Carrier Shipment Details report
has been improved with
both carrier rates and markup rates (which make up the total rate) now defined at the Carrier setup.
What's Fixed
For
Techship
, we can now
send confirmations for Saturday delivery, international billing types, residential addresses, and company names successfully.
When using the
Batch Label Printing at the Packing Station
feature, the system was
overriding the Carrier and Shipping Option
fields with the selections from the first order packed on the screen. Now, the system will
consider the Carrier and Shipping Option selected on the Shipment Order
when utilizing Batch Label Printing at the Packing Station.
In response to the issue where the
Received Quantity field was inaccurately updated when multiple pack types were received in a purchase order
, the following changes have been implemented:
Column names have been changed and updated
to add clarification.
The
calculation logic for the receiving difference has been modified
to accurately account for numerous pack types.
The
Total Quantity fields at Mobile Receiving were displaying incorrect values when higher-level pack types were included or received in a purchase order
. Pack type quantities will now be converted to unit of measure quantities.
As the
PO Qty
box has caused some confusion for users during receiving,
this field has been removed from all receiving related screens.
Some
custom field toggles were sending incorrect values
(showing them false/disabled rather than not active/null) on the backend. This issue has been resolved.
Send Email workflow action updates:
The
variables/placeholders list was not visible for users.
This has been adjusted, so users can now see their options to use when creating workflows for sending emails, such as {{warehouseCode}}
Example:
If {{warehouseCode}} is added to the mail body,
the workflow will replace the placeholder with the
Warehouse Code
information from the system.
Some
email placeholders were not functioning correctly
. All placeholders should now be working as expected.
The
Serial Number Tracking Report has been adjusted to check for client, warehouse, and user access.
Now, if a user does not have access to a given client or warehouse,
they will not be able to view the serial number of a SKU that they do not have access to.
An issue with
customer names with only one name defined
(e.g. customers with only a first or last name entered)
not displaying at the Packing screen
has been resolved. Now,
names with only first or last names entered will display. If neither a first name or last name has been entered, a message will display "No customer defined."
The issue of
negative values in the Open PO Qty column on the ATP Report
has been resolved.
API/Webhooks
A new
Create VAS Operations Bulk endpoint has been added to Logiwa's Open API.
This endpoint allows external services to
add multiple VAS logs with active VAS types.
A
Client Official Name
field has been
added to all Billing GET methods.
A
Billing Report Update
endpoint
had been added to the system, through which users can update the
Billing Status and IsExported columns at the Billing Report screen
.
An
IsExported column has been added to the Billing Report endpoints
, to allow users to filter and track exported billing reports.
Updates for the following endpoints now
allow the automatic creation and assignment of third-party accounts when shipment orders are accepted via API:
Create Shipment Order
Create Shipment Orders in Bulk
Get Shipment Order
List Shipment Order
Update Shipment Order
Update Shipment Order in Bulk
Couldn’t Find What You Were Looking For?
Visit our
Help Center
to search for more documents!

03/06/2024 Release Notes
06/05/2024 Release Notes
08/06/2024 Release Notes

title: 01/04/2024 Release Notes
content:
What’s New/Improved
It is now possible to utilize pre-defined custom fields of the various modules (shipment order, product, location, LP type) on the workflow, algorithms & carrier label messages.
We have a new parameter for Serial Number Tracking in the Product settings:

If there is a problem with the imported serial numbers, there is the option to delete Serial numbers (Delete Serial Numbers from Purchase Order screen) and import again.

New fields have been added to the Location setup screen:

. These fields are available in the interface, Location Excel import sheets, and related Open API endpoints.
Wave Rules grid can be filtered by the

and

parameters now!

.
